I purchased a vehicle on 26th November 2025.  Along with the expensive platinum warranty for 2 years you are highly encouraged to buy....

Within 1 week I was driving the car back...1 hr journey.  All wheels needed balancing, and a tyre completely replaced, along with a new electric window motor for rear drivers passenger.  Yes, 1 hr drive in rain with window open on a motorway.  Yay !!

The response...sorry Zowie you know used cars we can't know these things before you take the car....

All wheels needing to be rebalanced and a new tyre not being picked up before sale.....hmmmm.

Was the car fixed, yes.

Now its April 2026.  Huge issue.

Red warning.  Do not drive car, suspension fault detected.

The vehicle was leaking fluid from nearside rear.  Fluid all over driveway.  Underneath shows a pipe completely saturated.

Message sent to Jack Henry.

' yeah sorry Zowie you know these things happen with used cars, you have your platinum warranty. So youll have to use that.  Get the car recovered....yes thats not covered by your warranty....then see what the garage says and hopefully youll be covered...'

Vehicle purchased Ranger Rover Sport Autobiography £33000 approx.

No. No warranty.

This is a Consumer Rights Act 2015 issue.

I have had various emails with Josh the operations manager.  Who repeatedly tells me to use my warranty.

Citizens Advice and trading standards are now involved.

And Jack Henry are now 1 week into their 14 day notice period.

A vehicle purchased within 6 months under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 must be repaired or replaced by the seller.  At no cost or inconvenience to the customer.  They have 1 attempt at repair to a satisfactory standard.  If not the customer is entitled to a full refund.

I have been told I have been passed to Joshs Manager.

I have not heard from him.

Note to new customers.....

If you buy a car be prepared to buy the warranty, because then they can sell defective cars with no financial comeback.

If you wish to ask me questions  ill be happy to answer.

And once I have received a reply from Jack Henry and a resolution I will happily post it here.
Zowie Carr

one_star_reviews.text: I chose this place for my 9 year old’s piercings because of the fantastic reviews, but our experience didn’t live up to others’ and I feel more upset about it the further I get. She also was quite clumsy on my daughter’s second ear - the clamp kept falling off. I was surprised she wasn’t more adept and swift after the child knows the pain of the first one. Also, the head of her left piercing fell off after two weeks. Luckily we were able to find it, re-sterilise it, and screw it back on without a tool (this also involved having to poke the stem back through a little bit, which was very painful). A gem on the right piercing fell out after three weeks. I’m surprised by this because the earrings - and the whole thing - were ludicrously expensive. The price is about triple that of a reputable tattoo parlour (where I now wish we’d gone). The website makes it look like a spa but it’s a residential address and more like a bedroom. The spray that you have to buy afterwards has no ingredients list. Overall, I feel duped. Nasila is nice, and I am sad to have to leave a review like this, but there are too many aspects I feel are worth mentioning to other parents. The positive thing is that they haven’t become infected.

I’ve been studying at this college since September 2025, currently enrolled in a Level 3 IT course, and I want to give an honest and balanced review based on my experience so far.

Unfortunately, the course has been quite disorganised. One of the main issues is that coursework is not consistently checked or reviewed by teachers, which makes it difficult to know whether I’m on the right track or meeting the required standards. This lack of feedback has made it harder to stay confident in my progress.

Another concern is the high turnover of staff. So far, around three teachers from the course have already left, which has disrupted learning and made it difficult to maintain continuity. It also raises concerns about stability within the department.

In addition, classroom environments are often very noisy and lack structure. Lessons can sometimes feel more like social spaces rather than focused learning environments, which makes it difficult to concentrate and stay productive. Personally, this has started to impact my mental wellbeing, as the overall environment can feel quite chaotic and overwhelming at times.

There are also concerns regarding the bursary system. The financial support provided seems limited, as it is mainly based on distance rather than individual circumstances. I have personally had to pay for transport, including Ubers to get to college, and these costs are not adequately covered.

More importantly, I have an EHCP, which should entitle me to additional financial support of around £1,200 per year as part of being in a vulnerable group. However, despite this, the college bursary team has refused to provide this support. This has been particularly frustrating, as the purpose of this funding is to support students who need extra help to access education.

To be fair, the college does have potential, but significant improvements are needed — particularly in staff consistency, classroom management, student support, and fair access to financial assistance.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously, as it reflects genuine concerns that could improve the experience for current and future students.

Yesterday I had a very upsetting experience at Decathlon Canada Water that I believe should be taken seriously.

While trying bicycles for my 6-year-old nephew, we suddenly realised our 3-year-old child was no longer with us. For a few terrifying moments we could not find him anywhere, before eventually discovering that he had managed to walk out of the store alone without security noticing. Thankfully, we found him safely outside the store.

Any family with small children will understand how frightening those moments are. In most large stores, security would normally notice or stop a child under five years old leaving alone without an adult nearby. This is a basic safety expectation many parents naturally have in large public retail environments.

After finding the child, I respectfully raised my concern with security. The security guard I spoke with was polite and apologetic. However, another employee working there behaved in an extremely aggressive and inappropriate manner, shouting loudly in front of young children and then beginning to mock the situation instead of handling it professionally.

I know many of the staff working in the Canada Water area because I personally run several businesses locally, which made this experience even more disappointing and upsetting for me.

I will be formally following this matter up beyond this review, because no one should feel comfortable behaving this way in front of small children during an already stressful situation for a family.

I hope this incident is properly reviewed, because families with young children should feel safe and treated with respect in environments like this.

I am extremely disappointed with the service I received from this dealership and the owner karl. After trading in two vehicles as part of a purchase agreement, the dealer failed to notify the DVLA of the change of keeper. Weeks later, I received official correspondence confirming that I am still recorded as the keeper of both vehicles, which are now showing as untaxed and uninsured — despite the fact that they have been in the dealer’s possession since the day of the trade‑in.

To make matters worse, the dealer karl refused to allow us access to our own V5C documents. We had to repeatedly chase for updates and even return to the showroom in person just to try to get the V5C documents (it appears he has done this multiple times). Despite all of this, the DVLA was still never notified.

This failure has exposed me to potential fines, enforcement action, and legal liability for vehicles I do not own or control. We also have evidence that both vehicles remain on the dealer’s forecourt, making the lack of DVLA notification completely unacceptable. (we have now received fines from the DVLA for both cars and the owner Karl is nowhere to be seen)

Ensuring DVLA updates is a basic legal responsibility for any motor trader. The lack of communication, accountability, and proper administration has caused unnecessary stress, inconvenience and financial penalty. I am now having to escalate the matter to DVLA Enforcement, Trading Standards, and legal advisers.
Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this dealership and would advise anyone to Avoid at all costs.

one_star_reviews.text:
Looking for a new place to live? Think twice about Rochester Place.

My partner and I moved into a flat in Harringay in September 2024. Our initial interactions with the agency were pleasant, but the experience quickly deteriorated.

When we moved in, the flat had multiple issues including dirty floors, damage to the walls, a dysfunctional kitchen and a broken wardrobe door with a loose glass panel.

A few months later, large areas of black mould began appearing on the walls. We reported it immediately, but were told no tenant had complained in the previous four years and that the issue must be caused by us. Around the same time, I developed ongoing respiratory problems and my GP suggested damp and mould exposure could have been a contributing factor.

We bought an industrial dehumidifier ourselves, which showed humidity levels of 86% and regularly filled its tank twice per day. Despite regular ventilation, recurring leaks in the kitchen and walls that would often “sweat”, the agency continued to insist the issue was our responsibility and refused to bring in a specialist.

It also became clear we were not the only flat affected by damp issues after a neighbour’s bathroom floor partially collapsed due to rot underneath.

Other maintenance problems throughout the tenancy included repeated issues with the shower and a broken oven. In our opinion, repairs were often incomplete or delayed.

Before moving out, we agreed to extend the tenancy slightly while waiting to complete on a property purchase. The agency agreed provided we accepted a £100 rent increase and left a positive Google review, which we never did.

At the end of the tenancy, despite leaving the flat in a much better condition than when we moved in, the agency attempted to deduct money from our deposit for cleaning and mould-related issues. We disputed the deductions through the deposit scheme.

I have rented several flats in London and never previously felt the need to leave a review for an estate agency, but this experience genuinely stood out for the wrong reasons. Based on our experience, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

Genuinely disappointed with how Rai handled a simple rescheduling request and I think other diners should know what happened before booking.
I had a lunch booked for two on the 13th of May at 12:30. My client had to reschedule on the morning of, so I tried to call the restaurant three times to move it, with no answer on any of the calls. I then emailed asking to move the booking to the 27th of May at the same time. Same group, same spend, just a different date. Effectively I was bringing the same business back to them two weeks later.
Their response was to apply a £150 charge (£75 per person), treating a date change as if it were a cancellation. Even after I made the case that I was rescheduling and not cancelling, that I was a returning local customer who had recommended them to others, and that I had tried to call multiple times before any deadline, they refused to budge.
A few things worth flagging for anyone considering booking:

£75 per person for a date change is well above the London norm. £10 to £25 per head is standard for last-minute changes at restaurants of any tier, including Michelin-starred ones.
The restaurant repeatedly described itself as a "small independent" while simultaneously deflecting every decision to a "Head Office" they would not put me in touch with or escalate the matter to.
Once I formally asked for escalation, communication went silent and the £150 charge was processed without any further reply.

The food and atmosphere on previous visits had been good, which is why this is a real let-down. But the policy enforcement and the customer service when something goes wrong are both worth knowing about before you commit. Will not be back, and I would think twice before booking somewhere whose response to a genuine rescheduling request is a £150 charge and silence.

Zero stars if I could. I never ate here — and after this experience, I never will.
I needed to cancel a reservation 47 hours ahead of time — one hour inside their 48-hour policy. The website wouldn't let me cancel online. No one answered the phone. The next morning I was told to write to head office. The outcome? They kept my £150 deposit without any offer of flexibility or compromise.

What frustrates me most is how simple the solution was: let me rebook. They keep the deposit, I still visit — everyone wins. Instead, they chose to take the money and lose the customer.

RAI is a corporate chain, and it shows. There is no personal touch, no goodwill, and no interest in the customer beyond their deposit. Plenty of exceptional sushi restaurants in London genuinely care about their guests. This is not one of them. Spend your money somewhere that will.

I chose Montrose Clinic based on its 5-star reviews and initially felt confident booking. I went in to treat pigmentation and was advised that BBL would be a suitable option, with a course of three sessions recommended alongside a very expensive ZO Skin routine.

After two sessions and over £2,000 spent on treatments and skincare (which I used for months), I saw no improvement in my pigmentation, so I did not proceed with the third session. I have generally very good skin with no history of acne or scarring, my only concern was pigmentation. I also have a medium skin tone and am aware caution is needed with BBL on tanned skin, which the clinic were aware of from the start and still advised me to proceed. The skincare I was recommended led to breakouts and marks I had not experienced before.

I raised both the lack of results and my reaction to the products during my visits. Despite this, I later felt the lack of results was being attributed to me not using retinol, even though I had explained my skin was already reacting to the products I had been advised to use.

The only solution presented to me was to move on to a stronger laser (Halo), even at a discounted rate. The offer of a free patch test only came after I questioned why I should spend more money when the initial treatment had not worked. I went ahead with the free patch test and saw no difference in my pigmentation, and had I not pushed back on further spend, I would have ended up paying even more for the same outcome. After seeing no difference from the patch test, I told the clinic I would be happy to come in again if there was a solution that did not involve spending more money after the previous treatments had not worked for me, but I never received a response to that.

I also referred my sister to the clinic, which makes the experience even more disappointing.

I am now left with scars I have not experienced before, no improvement in pigmentation, and significant money spent without results. While the team are polite, there was no meaningful reassessment when the treatment wasn’t working, other than being directed towards spending more money.

I hope this helps others avoid the mistakes I made.

I joined Triyoga Chelsea in Nov 2024, and initially it was a lovely studio with a great range of yoga classes across three well-sized spaces with some excellent teachers. The environment was clean, calm, and welcoming, and the staff were always friendly.
However, early last year the studio was reconfigured to include a reformer Pilates space. This reduced the number of yoga classes and significantly changed the overall atmosphere.
Classes became more crowded in a smaller studio, and the noise from the reformer sessions made it difficult to enjoy what should be a peaceful experience. Despite this, I remained a member for some time, as there were still enough classes I could attend.
Following further cancellations of those classes, I decided to cancel my membership and gave notice in person on 1 March. I was asked when I wanted it to end, and I said the end of the month, assuming this would align with my billing date on the 29th. I was told this would be fine.
I was therefore surprised to be charged again on 29th March for April. When I queried this, I was informed 30 days' notice is required as per the contract. While I don't dispute this, it had been well over a year since I signed this agreement, and I would have expected this to be clearly pointed out at the time of cancellation.
I contacted the manager to ask whether the charge could be waived as a gesture of goodwill but received an unhelpful response referring strictly to 'company policy'. As a result, I have effectively been charged an additional month due to a one-day discrepancy. Whilst this may be contractually correct, it feels unreasonable and disappointing from a customer service perspective.
Overall, it's disappointing to have had to cancel due to the reduction in classes, and this final experience has left a particularly negative impression. My overall rating is O stars!

I used to really enjoy coming to this yoga studio.  However, since merging with the Pilates studio, it no longer feels like a dedicated yoga space. During Sunday meditation sessions, it’s difficult to relax due to noise coming through the thin wall from the Pilates classes next door (the situation is similar for other classes as well). It’s also disappointing that many of my favourite instructors have left, they used to come up and correct everyone even if it was a very busy class. The current class schedule isn’t convenient for those working at least 9-6. Overall, a lot of confusion with the booking new app and everything. I cancelled my membership. PS I also requested for my membership to remain active until 14th April (and I have an email to confirm that), but it appears it was cancelled early on 14th March, which is frustrating and not what I had asked for.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited this jeweller in Kingsbury (NW9 9DT) on 14th March to order a custom ring — a gold band with two lab diamonds — at a quoted price of £830. I was told it would be ready within two weeks, which would have been 28th March.

By that date, I had received no update or communication. I called to check on the status, and the response I received was abrupt and dismissive. I was simply told to wait until they contacted me, which I accepted at the time as I was only seeking a basic update.

On 30th March, having still heard nothing, I sent a message asking for an update. This message was ignored. I was then contacted on 3rd April and told that “the ring” was ready for collection, without any clarity on which ring they were referring to (as I had placed more than one order). When I asked for clarification, I received no response and had to call again myself. During that call, I was told it was the gold band with the two lab diamonds.

I requested a photo of the ring before travelling and also asked whether my other ring would be ready so I could collect both at once. The response I received was again abrupt and unhelpful, simply stating that only one was ready. When I followed up to ask about the timeline for the second ring — which was a simple adjustment and should not have taken longer than two weeks — I was ignored again.

On 4th April, I was told both rings were ready for collection. However, when I arrived the same day, the custom gold band with the lab diamonds had been made incorrectly. The diamonds were positioned in a way that meant they would be hidden under my engagement ring, despite all measurements having been provided clearly at the time of order. I was told it would need to be remade, requiring an additional two weeks. While this was frustrating, I remained patient and simply asked them to correct the ring as originally agreed. No clear timeline was provided at this stage.

On 11th April, I called again to request an update. Instead of receiving reassurance or a progress update, I was met with attitude and told that it had “only been a week,” despite the delays already exceeding the original agreed timeframe. The conversation ended with them telling me to come and collect my deposit, which I ultimately agreed to, as I no longer felt confident continuing with them.

The entire experience was disappointing from start to finish. What should have been a meaningful and exciting process — creating wedding bands with my partner — turned into a stressful and frustrating ordeal due to poor communication, missed timelines, and consistently unprofessional customer service.

Additionally, during my initial visit, a staff member recorded a conversation between myself and my mother about the ring design without asking for consent. This was extremely uncomfortable and inappropriate. When I raised it, the response was dismissive, saying it would not be used if I didn’t want it to be — which completely misses the point that consent should have been obtained beforehand.

I also noticed inconsistent customer service. While we were there discussing our order, other customers were offered refreshments and treated warmly, whereas we were met with a noticeably colder and less attentive approach. This inconsistency only added to the overall negative experience.

In summary, this was the worst experience I have had with a jeweller. The lack of communication, failure to meet agreed timelines, poor workmanship on the initial attempt, and unprofessional behaviour from staff made this an experience I would not recommend. I ended up going and getting my deposit back and Alhamdulliah I will not be returning.

Innocent shoppers beware. It could be you next

On 26 January 2026, at approximately 7:00pm GMT, I was approached by a security guard at the Fenwick store in Brent Cross Shopping Centre (men’s clothing department) and informed that I was “banned” from the store. At the time, I was simply browsing on my own. I am relieved I was not accompanied by anyone, as the situation would have been even more embarrassingu. I was in shock and asked for an explanation. However, the guard provided no proper explanation and insisted that he “recognised” me. I immediately asked to speak to the manager on duty. It later became apparent—although no one actually explained this to me—that he had mistaken me for someone else and wrongly associated me with a previous shoplifting incident. I can only guess as I have never been involved in a crime in my life. Never shop lifted. Something to with the baby department or something. I don’t even have kids but he was vague when I asked I was banned for what

I was then made to wait for more than fifteen minutes while staff discussed the situation. When the manager finally approached me, she asked me to explain what had happened, despite the fact that the security guard had already confronted me and claimed I was banned. Given the circumstances, I would have expected the explanation to come from them, not the other way around. Her handling of the situation demonstrated a complete lack of professionalism, decency, empathy, and basic people skills. She did not apologise, offer reassurance, or take any responsibility for the distress caused. At one point she even asked me “well, what do you want me to do about it?”. it’s this sort of behaviour that can negatively impact the reputation of companies that hire them.

Instead, I was told to “go on my way,” as though the situation were insignificant. There was no acknowledgement of the mistake, no explanation, and no consideration for the impact this had on me. When I asked whether she was the most senior manager available, she confirmed that she was.

To be clear, my complaint is not about the security guard. I understand that their job is challenging, especially given the rise in shoplifting in recent years. People make mistakes but he could have handled the situation better. My concern is with the manager’s response and the unacceptable way the entire situation was handled from start to finish. Three Fenwick staff discussing the situation as I hung around did not help matters either.

This incident has had a genuinely negative impact on me. I will not be shopping at Fenwick again, nor will I be entering the store in the future. I will also be advising family and friends to be cautious, as no customer should ever be subjected to such treatment.

I have shared my experience with several people, and all of them agree with me and understand why I was so shaken up. It is also very disappointing, as Fenwick has always been one of my favourite stores. Not any more. My family will no longer shop in any of their stores either when I explained the situation. I now feel uncomfortable even walking into Fenwick so don't.

I would like to acknowledge the gentleman who assisted me in locating the manager; he was the only staff member who demonstrated any sense of support or courtesy. I would strongly suggest that the manager involved seek guidance from colleagues like him on how to handle sensitive situations with professionalism and respect

While I accept that the security guard made an honest mistake, the manager’s behaviour only intensified the situation rather than resolving it. Her conduct was unacceptable.
In summary, this incident stands as a textbook example of how not to handle a situation involving a customer. From the initial misidentification to the complete absence of accountability, communication, or basic courtesy, every stage of this interaction reflected a failure of judgment and leadership.

It’s now April 2026. I complained to  back in January. Still waiting for an explanation. None received. I still don’t shop in their store and I refuse to do so.

Booked a Maldives package through Lastminute.com for several thousand pounds and this has been one of the most frustrating customer service experiences I’ve had.
Etihad Airways changed our flight, increasing the stopover from 1 hour 40 minutes to 7 hours 30 minutes, and directed us to the agent to resolve it.
We are now expected to travel from London to Abu Dhabi and then remain in transit for over 7 hours with a 2-year-old, after an already long flight, while also losing valuable, fully paid resort time.
Lastminute’s response has been to describe this as a “minor change”. Customer service has been dismissive, unhelpful, and lacking any real consideration for the impact, particularly when travelling with a young child.
This is not a minor adjustment. It materially changes the journey, affects a family with a toddler, and reduces the value of a holiday we have paid thousands for.
What is most concerning is the lack of ownership. The airline directs you to the agent, and the agent minimises the issue. As a customer, you are left without meaningful support.
I would strongly caution others, particularly families travelling with young children, to consider carefully before booking through Lastminute.com.
Unless this is resolved appropriately, I will be escalating this via ABTA and the CAA.

My experience with lastminute was beyond frustrating and completely unacceptable.

The airline changed our flight to Malé, turning a 1 hour 30 minute stopover into a ridiculous 7 hour 45 minute wait due to “operational changes.” Not only were we not contacted to discuss options, but the change was somehow “accepted” without my authorisation. Customer service then had the audacity to claim I agreed to it despite clear email evidence showing otherwise.

I was also told that Etihad Airways considers this a “minor change.” Let’s be clear: adding over 6 extra hours to a layover while travelling with a 2-year-old is not minor, it’s a major disruption.

Customer support made the situation even worse. The live chat agent was unhelpful, and the phone agent was outright rude. There was laughing in the background, a dismissive tone throughout, and clear frustration when I questioned incorrect advice. I was even told to contact Etihad directly despite booking through lastminute, which shows a complete lack of understanding of their own responsibilities.

When a “solution” was finally offered, it came with impatience and poor attitude, as if helping a customer was an inconvenience

I won’t be using lastminute again. Poor communication, zero accountability, and shockingly bad customer service, avoid if you value your time, money, and sanity.

I am extremely disappointed with the way this business has handled a very serious situation. My phone was stolen while I was on the premises, and despite reporting the incident and following up multiple times via email, I have received absolutely no response. The complete lack of communication and accountability is unacceptable, especially given the seriousness of theft on their property.

At the very least, I expected a timely reply, some form of investigation, or even basic customer support. Instead, I have been ignored entirely, which gives the impression that customer safety and concerns are not taken seriously here. This experience has caused me significant inconvenience and stress, and the lack of support has only made matters worse.

What is even more concerning is the safeguarding aspect. This is a place where parents bring their children and, in many cases, leave them in the care of staff or teachers. If incidents like theft are not properly addressed and there is no clear communication or response from management, it raises serious concerns about how well the environment is being monitored and how safe it truly is for children. A lack of responsiveness in such matters could potentially put young people at risk.

Businesses have a responsibility not only to provide a service but also to ensure a safe and secure environment for everyone, especially children. Ignoring customers in situations like this is both unprofessional and irresponsible. I strongly urge others to be cautious, and I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves their handling of safety, safeguarding, and customer concerns in the future.

I wanted to write this review because the overwhelmingly positive feedback online does not reflect my experience over the nearly eight months I was at Roar. I think it’s important that prospective clients, especially those who feel vulnerable or lack confidence around their weight-loss journey, have a fuller picture for balance.

Roar presents itself as a premium weight-loss transformation service with tailored nutrition and a high level of personalised support. In my experience, that was not what I received. While the gym itself is polished and the environment feels premium, for me the justification for the price largely ended there.

Overall, the service felt more transactional than transformational. The marketing is compelling, but the wider support required for genuine, lasting change felt limited. There seemed to be little real understanding of the psychological and emotional challenges that often come with weight loss, which can be deeply disappointing for clients expecting meaningful encouragement, accountability, and empathy.

The “tailored nutrition support” was especially poor. In practice, it felt more like a generic recipe pack than proper education on how to eat in a healthy, sustainable, and adaptable way. There was very little focus on building long-term understanding or habits. Over time, the appointments became so unhelpful and off-putting, particularly because of certain inappropriate comments and the uncomfortable calliper body-measurement sessions, that I stopped attending them altogether despite having already paid for them.

More broadly, there were repeated mismatches between what was promised during the onboarding consultation and what was actually delivered. The programme felt rigid, generic, and impersonal, with little room for genuine individual care beyond a standardised system. This may suit very self-motivated individuals, but for those seeking truly tailored support, it falls short.

I also found the overall service lacked continuity. I left having achieved only part of a significant weight-loss journey and received no follow-up or check-in from leadership or management. For a company positioning itself as a life-changing transformation service, that was disappointing.

I’m sharing this not out of malice, but out of honesty. In my opinion, Roar did not provide the supportive, personalised transformation environment its marketing led me to expect, and prospective clients should ask very direct questions before committing.

Furthermore it is poor practice by pubs to charge a service charge, even if it is discretionary, for simply serving drinks at the bar. If it is table service, then of course it is justified.

I’ll start by saying that dining at Fat Crab is definitely billed as "an experience" – but for me, it was one I won’t be repeating, and I can’t in good conscience recommend it to anyone who prefers eating with plates and cutlery, or who has dietary needs like lactose intolerance.

Let’s address the positives first: the shellfish is fresh – you can tell that much from the texture and smell of the prawns and mussels when they arrive. But that’s where the good points end for me. As someone who can’t have dairy, I was disappointed to learn there are absolutely no sauces available that cater to lactose intolerance – everything on offer is cream-based, so the food came out pretty bland with no way to add any flavor or moisture.

What really threw me off was the approach to dining basics. When I realized they weren’t bringing any plates at all, I politely asked if I could at least have some cutlery. The staff looked at me like I was from another planet, and then made a rather rude comment saying it was "impossible" to use cutlery for shelled king prawns and mussels. Even if they don’t typically use utensils to eat their own food, there’s no need to make customers feel awkward or judge their preferences – that kind of comment is unnecessary and comes across as dismissive.

But what’s truly unforgivable is that the prawns weren’t properly cleaned – their intestines were still intact and visible. I understand their concept is serving food in bags, and I can even overlook that they haven’t thought through non-dairy seasoning options, but dirty shellfish is a basic food preparation issue that simply shouldn’t happen in any restaurant. It’s not just unappetizing – it raises serious questions about attention to detail and food safety standards.

I gave the place a chance to live up to the hype and tried the "experience" once. But between the lack of dietary options, the rude response to reasonable requests, and most importantly, improperly prepared seafood, I won’t be going back. If you’re someone who likes to eat off plates, use cutlery, or expects shellfish to be properly cleaned and seasoned to suit different needs, this isn’t the spot for you.

A one-time experience — and that was enough.

Our experience with The Knowledge Academy in connection with a Minitab training course was extremely disappointing overall.

After our very first non-binding enquiry, we were contacted almost daily, sometimes several times a day, and repeatedly pushed to make a decision, even though it had been clearly communicated that internal decision-making at a university takes time. We found this sales approach far too aggressive.

On top of that, the final offer initially showed a price that was roughly double the amount previously discussed and had to be corrected. The participant contract also included a flex option under which one postponement of the training week was supposed to be free of charge. However, when we needed to move the training by just one week, we were suddenly told that an additional 70% would be charged. Only after extensive back-and-forth emails and the involvement of our commercial department was it finally clarified that this extra charge would not apply.

The most frustrating part was the short-notice change of the training location. This was justified by referring to the terms and conditions, which apparently allow The Knowledge Academy to change the venue at short notice. Regardless of whether this may be covered contractually, it caused significant extra time and expense for me. My hotel had already been booked based on the original arrangement, and because the new location was much farther away on the outskirts of London, I had to spend around two and a half extra hours per day travelling during the first days.

The overall lab / virtual desktop setup also felt chaotic. Although I had booked a professional training course, I was simply sent links without any proper explanation or guidance. What made this even worse was the contrast in communication: while they were trying to win me as a customer, I received repeated phone calls; when I later had concrete questions about logging in and using the system, it took days to get a response. Even then, a different person replied each time, although I had contacted my original point of contact directly.

The only genuinely positive part of this experience was the trainer. He was understanding, flexible, and willing to meet me at my hotel rather than insist on the newly assigned venue, which made a difficult situation much more manageable.

The original purpose of this booking was also to assess whether The Knowledge Academy in London would be a suitable provider for future training of other professors and research staff from our university. After this experience, that is completely out of the question for us.

Overall, we were left with the impression of aggressive sales behaviour, poor organisation, inconsistent communication, and a process that did not feel reliable or customer-oriented. Based on our experience, we cannot recommend The Knowledge Academy.

Usually, I refrain from giving bad reviews, but this one is completely necessary!!!!!
I’ve never applied to work for Claibon, but I was contacted and offered the job by one of their recruitment consultants- Christina Wride via the CV library. At first instance, they seemed ok, so I thought I would give it a go.
However, my experience with this agency was awful. From the beginning, communication was a disaster even though shifts were handed out, there was little to no information, when I was already at the job it was often completely different from what was originally described.
What made things even worse was the toxic and hostile work environment at some of their client's sites. For example, I experienced bullying at one of the placements and when I reported it to the agency, their response was somehow dismissive. This happened also at another site of theirs. What was more shocking is that the permanent concierge I worked with was one of their former employees. A girl who could barely speak any English was rude to bits not only to me but to residents as well. This was to my biggest surprise the most abrupt conduct I’ve ever seen. After I confronted her my shifts were cancelled. Here the agency instead of supporting me, took the client’s side and made excuses, claiming they were not aware of this before or that the company managers and staff were ‘stressed’, or subtly implying that I wasn’t good enough for the job—even though I had done nothing wrong and was simply trying to work in a professional environment. If a shift gets cancelled, rather than taking responsibility or offering proper reasoning, they’ll blame the worker instead of acknowledging the real issue.
The recruitment consultants themselves are shockingly rude and unprofessional. They speak to staff in a condescending tone (Charlie, Anna, Clair, and others I can’t remember all their names), treating workers with little to no respect. Any concerns raised are brushed off, and they make it clear they have no interest in fair treatment—only in keeping their clients happy at the expense of their workers. No wonder they are constantly looking for staff!!!
To add to the list of red flags, they are completely exploitative when it comes to pay they are paying the minimum wage. For a 12-hour shift, their clients are charged almost tripple with VAT, yet the worker only gets £147 while Claibon pockets same amount even more —almost half of what the company pays! And for all that money they take, they provide zero support when problems arise. Considering how disrespectful they are towards their staff is absurd!!!!
On top of that, instead of improving their service, they even ask staff via lame emails to leave fake 5-star positive Google reviews in exchange for more shifts (I’ve included a screenshot of that email below)—a desperate attempt to cover up their bad reputation instead of fixing their core issues. Honestly, who would do that ????? From first-hand experience, I assure you this is how they’ve got all their 5-star reviews here!!!
They don’t care about the well-being of their workers, only about filling roles as quickly as possible!!!!! Also, what is more miserable and pathetic about them is that i did give them clear  message that i no longer wish to work for this toxic organisation etc. But they are so desperate so keep calling me every single day at least 3 times , i totally ignore them!!!
If you want to be treated with respect, fairness, and professionalism, please Avoid this agency!!!
They are disorganized, exploitative, and do not care about their workers. There are far better agencies out there—don’t waste your time with this one!!!!

Awful living environment and irresponsible housekeeping staffs. After futile efforts filing complaints to the accommodation team, their lack of action has left me with no choice but to write this honest review:

They claim that there is housekeeping every day from Monday to Friday. However, in reality, the cleaner is usually only available a couple of days, and then he is absent for many days e.g. taking a whole week off, often leaving the whole house uncleaned for 2 consecutive weeks. He is frequently on annual leave (and he does so during times when there is a high need for cleaning) with NO ONE REPLACING his shift, which is unreasonable given the number of people needing his work daily. This leaves the trash bins full and the floors/tables uncleaned, growing pests and strange smells, with construction dust and dirt all over the carpets in the corridors. How irresponsible is that.

The construction noise is killing me. Constructors have left so much dusts on my 19th-century big old windows that getting a breath of fresh air is often difficult. Everyday the four walls of my room vibrate with brutal noise. I woke up in the LOUD chatting and noises everyday at 8 AM and could only escape outside to find some peace. The construction work was said to be completed by February, but it is still ongoing now in April. Extremely unreliable and inefficient.

As if we haven’t breathed in enough dust and paint from this construction site, they comfortably left the house uncleaned and untidied most of the time... They should find replacements to make up for the significant amount of missed housekeeping shifts. Unironically this is the bare minimum for any standard accommodation...

I should not need to send countless emails chasing them up to do the housekeeping work they promised to provide. This is opposed to what I agreed on, and paid tens of thousands of pounds for! They really should have compensated me for all my sufferings from the noise and horrid conditions this year.

There are countless other issues, such as failing to prevent homeless people from entering the house freely, leading to stolen food items of mine totalling around £15. However, the problem that haunted me for the longest time has been the inadequate housekeeping services and how little they care about keeping the house cleaned and well-maintained during this dust-inducing construction period.

I am going to keep this reviews active and I will follow up on whether they're resolving these ongoing problems.

I paid over £3,000 for a comprehensive package with “unlimited refinements.” Despite going through three refinement stages, my teeth are still uneven, my jaw feels misaligned, and I have ongoing pain in a front tooth. I raised these issues multiple times but they were never properly addressed.

I was eventually offered either one final refinement or £1,000 towards another clinic. I declined further refinements as previous attempts hadn’t worked, and I don’t think it’s fair to pay more elsewhere to fix these issues.

Additionally, the retainers provided after each stage didn’t fit properly, which I also reported several times.

Overall, the experience has been stressful and upsetting, and my teeth are worse than before I started. I would not recommend this clinic.

Dropped my car off on 8th April for a locking issue. I was told it may need to be kept overnight to strip it down. After multiple weeks of chasing for updates with no clear answers, I eventually went away as there was no end in sight.

Throughout the whole period I was never given a clear timeframe or explanation for the delay. On multiple occasions I was told I’d hear back the next day, but no one ever called - I always had to follow up myself.

The fault turned out to be the body control module, which I accept. The car was eventually collected on 29th April.

On collection we found a McDonald’s bag with old food inside and a receipt dated 20th April in the passenger footwell, from a branch in Enfield - two days before the car was declared ready on 22nd April.

The car does appear to be fixed, but based on the experience I wouldn’t return or recommend.

I hired their services to pour a concrete slab inside my house. I requested 10mm aggregate but when they invoiced me, it was stating 20mm mix. When I pointed it out they lied and said it was 10mm and the invoice was wrong. Now, because the slab was very hard to level, I had to grind it down, and its obvious that is 20mm aggregate. Due to the aggregate being larger, when I done the pour I had a hard time leveling it correctly and now I have  to spend extra time and money to grind the concrete down. Also I had to pay for extra material (1 cubic meter) as it was more material going in due to it being hard to maneuver and level. Needles to say, I won't be using them again!
But I am concerned about the strength of my slab due to the 110mm thickness with 20mm aggregate.

Following the response from the owner, I have to reiterate the fact that I did complain to IMix at the time, email and phones but they simply didn't admit any wrong doing. They eventually provided cube tests which I didn't witnessed being done when the slab was poured. If the cubes were poured with my material, they would have seen the larger aggregates. Its just the whole behaviour being very shady and not trustworthy. I am downgrading to 1 star because of this.

one_star_reviews.text:
I chose this clinic because of its convenient location and advertised extended hours, including evenings and some Saturdays. From the beginning, I explained that I worked in an orthodontic clinic and was looking for an experienced, detail-oriented practitioner.

The first red flag was being sent an unencrypted invoice that wasn’t mine, which raised concerns about patient data handling. Despite this, I proceeded due to convenience. I was offered a very large discount on a comprehensive Invisalign package, which in hindsight may have influenced the provider I was assigned.

From the first appointments, I felt uncomfortable with the initial dentist. There was a lack of continuity and awareness. I often had to remind him of previous steps, and at times nurses appeared to guide him. During my IPR, he worked without assistance, and the result appears uneven, which raised concerns about safety and accuracy.

I requested a different dentist and was moved to someone more professional and precise. However, despite being on a comprehensive plan for maximum improvement, I was advised to finish after the initial aligners, which contradicted my consultation and required me to complain again.

Although I am happy with the Invisalign and bonding results, the main issue is inconsistency. It felt like the clinic prioritised availability and sales over matching me with the right clinician, possibly steering me toward a less in-demand practitioner with a discount I hadn’t asked for.

There were also misleading claims about availability. I was told there were evening and weekend options, but my dentist only worked 1–2 days a week, and poor scheduling caused delays throughout treatment.

The retention phase was poorly handled. Bonded retainers were placed without prior discussion, despite earlier advice against it for my case. I then had to wait 19 days for removable retainers with nothing to wear in between. The upper bonded retainer failed within an hour, and it was difficult to secure an emergency appointment.

Fortunately, another dentist at the clinic resolved the issue quickly and professionally, showing that there are excellent practitioners there.

In summary, the clinic has some very good dentists, but the quality of care is inconsistent. I would advise not relying solely on online reviews, and instead ensuring you are booked with a trusted and experienced practitioner.

I do have to ammend this review.

My dentist placed a bonded retainer on my upper arch in an area that he had previously said wouldn’t be suitable due to my malocclusion. He then scanned me with the bonded retainer in place and ordered three sets of retainers as part of my Invisalign package.

Unfortunately, the bonded retainer on my upper arch failed within one hour on Monday. I had an emergency appointment on Tuesday to remove the broken section. On Wednesday, I was given a temporary clear retainer thanks to Dr Patel, the only person who proactively helped maintain my results. By Thursday evening, more parts of the bonded retainer had failed.

Now it’s Good Friday, and I’m left with a loose, hanging retainer, unable to eat or speak properly during a long holiday weekend. This has caused significant discomfort and feels like a situation that could have been avoided.

Based on my experience, I would only recommend this clinic if you have a direct recommendation.

I will likely need to book a consultation with another clinic to correct any relapse and stabilise my results.

This was the worst security experience I’ve had at any venue. The moment we arrived, we were treated as if we were a threat, then detained inside under the pretense that the place was “maxed out” for crowd control. It felt like a deliberate tactic to create a false impression of a packed house, which is deceptive and manipulative. If the venue truly needed to limit entry, there should have been transparent communication, not a coercive hold that ruined the evening from the start.

The security team’s approach was inconsistent and overbearing. They shuttled people around, blocked exits, and made it virtually impossible to step outside for a cigarette without triggering a confrontation or a delay that killed the night. The whole “full house” justification came across as a manufactured obstacle rather than a legitimate safety measure. It’s one thing to enforce policies; it’s another to weaponize crowd control to trap guests inside and pressure them into staying.

Drinks were overpriced, which is unfortunately common, but it’s the combination with the security approach that makes the experience intolerable. When every dollar spent feels like it’s buying you a fight over basic access and comfort, it compounds the frustration. The price stings, but the bigger issue is how the venue treats its patrons: with suspicion, obstruction, and vague rules that change without notice.

The alcohol service and re-entry policy were poorly managed and poorly communicated. We were told one thing, then charged with another, and there was no clear guidance on what would allow us to come back after stepping outside. The lack of a coherent policy meant guests were left guessing and frequently blocked at the door or at the bar, creating needless delays and embarrassment. It’s unprofessional to govern guest behavior with mixed messages and arbitrary decisions.

Overall, the experience felt designed to extract as much money and as little courtesy as possible. The combination of deceptive crowd tactics, hard-to-navigate entry and re-entry rules, and inflated drink prices left a sour impression that lingered long after we left. Given how poorly this was managed, I have no plan to return, and I’ll caution others to reconsider before they book or attend.

If you are a prospective patient and being referred via another service or your GP, don't. Avoid being referred here. It is so incredibly overloaded that they are functionally incapable of treating new patients.

Even being discharged or referred elsewhere is a lengthy process, because they actually have to see you and evaluate you first, which as mentioned, can take up to a year.

Therefore referring yourself here is essentially the equivalent of not being treated. Capacity is so low that you will even struggle to get simple admin tasks like medication changes authorised if you are a long term patient here. At best, you will not receive treatment or will wait a very significant amount of time for it. At worst you could be endangering yourself.

Everyone understands the NHS is under significant pressure and staff are doing their best. However, the centre is unfit for practice. If it has not already, it could risk causing serious harm to its patients or even the general public.

The centre is chaotic. It is clearly managing far, far more patients than it is capable of and also managing many patients with complex mental health issues that require advanced support. However, as other reviews have detailed here, even a simple medication titration is a process that might take you 6 months or more (there is no way to contact the centre outside of your appointments). On that type of timeline, it could be multiple years before a patient who is referred here receives the correct treatment, and god knows the damage they could have done within that period.

When someone is seen, after perhaps waiting 9 or 10 months, the appointments are so short (5-10 minutes at times) that its hard to know what progress could even be made. I’m honestly quite surprised by the overwhelmingly positive reviews Habito receives. They’re great a littering great testimonials across their site and socials which we too, fell for.

We completed in December 2025 and, while the mortgage broker side of the service was good, our experience with Habito Plus/conveyancing was extremely disappointing.

Our legal team (who were paralegals rather than solicitors) failed to communicate key parts of the process to us and ignored important questions we raised. This resulted in us going through a simultaneous exchange and completion, something our estate agent had to inform us of on the actual day. Earlier in the process, our customer success representative had specifically mentioned that they wanted to avoid this scenario as it leaves buyers with less time to properly review commitments.

At one stage, our original conveyancer disappeared without explanation. It was only weeks later, after pressure from our estate agent, that Habito confirmed he had stepped away from the case and that the team was understaffed. In the end, about 4-5 people ended up being involved.

At the time, I considered making a complaint but decided against it as we just wanted to move on after completion. However, nearly six months later, we have now discovered that our property has two separate service charges to pay…something that should have been identified and clearly explained to us before completion. I’ve since contacted their post completion “expert” team, but unfortunately the lack of communication appears to be a recurring issue.

As first-time buyers purchasing a chain-free property, we did not expect such poor service from the legal side of the process. At several key stages, we felt unsupported and left in the dark. We often defended Habito throughout the purchase because they were acting on our behalf, which makes the overall experience even more disappointing in hindsight.

The one standout positive throughout all of this was Mariam, our customer success representative who was genuinely supportive. But to be frank, we didn’t just pay for that. The sad thing is this will review will probably get a response. I hope this provides a realistic start to end experience beneath all the 5 star reviews.

I’d strongly recommend keeping the review factual and evidence-based rather than “naming and shaming” individual employees personally. Publicly accusing named staff can backfire legally and weaken the credibility of your complaint.

A stronger approach is:

identify the company,

describe the documented failures,

mention first names only if necessary,

and stick strictly to verifiable facts from the email trail.

Here’s a strong version:

Extremely disappointing experience with Habito.

My remortgage application was mishandled over a period of nearly 3 months with repeated delays, conflicting updates, poor communication, and late-stage policy issues that should have been identified much earlier.

I was repeatedly reassured that the application was progressing towards offer, only to later discover directly from the lender that the application had already been declined the previous day while I was still being told there was “no update” and that the case was being actively chased.

There were multiple handovers between staff including Kurt, Anu, Scarlett and others, with continual back-and-forth, changing explanations, and avoidable delays throughout the process.

The most frustrating part is that the key lender policy issue appeared to have been visible from documentation held for a long time, yet it was only identified after months of work, stress, chasing, and wasted time.

I have now submitted formal complaints regarding the handling of the case.

Very disappointing experience overall.

Because the construction was so extensive this week, I went door to door at local businesses and determined it was Sedus who did the construction.

Never once have they provided warning of the works. It appears they are unconcerned with the fact that people live directly above where they are working, and only concerned with their own schedules and plans.

When I approached the business, they said it would just be 8-5 this week, yet the construction extended til close to 6pm yesterday. There was no acknowledgment of the fact they’ve been doing works on and off for months, mainly on evenings and weekends, and no recognition that their choices are impacting the people that live above their showroom.

I am not one to usually write reviews, however my experience with DLG Legal Services has been absolutely abysmal.

I was involved in a road traffic accident in late 2021 and, nearly five years later, my claim still remains unresolved despite the other driver admitting liability very early on. Throughout that time I have experienced repeated delays, multiple case handler changes and long periods with little meaningful communication or progress.

The most distressing issue, however, was the disclosure of a psychological report containing highly sensitive personal information. Medical and family-related information relating to myself and a family member was disclosed to someone who absolutely should not have received it, and the document was not adequately redacted. Additionally, said family member was also a completely separate data subject who was not involved in the claim and should not have been included in the report at all. The report contained deeply private information, including mental health history and family matters, which caused significant distress when disclosed.

I raised a formal complaint and provided detailed concerns, yet months later I am still waiting for a proper response addressing the issues raised. When I chased for a response to my complaint, I was told I was welcome to refer the matter to the Legal Ombudsman rather than receiving a substantive response. Being left to chase answers about both my claim and my complaint has only added to the frustration.

After years of delays, poor communication and the handling of sensitive information, I have lost complete confidence in the service provided. This has been an extremely stressful and disappointing experience.
Very unprofessional in their handling of a claim. Hope they go out of business and leave this to the professionals.

I had a very disappointing experience with DLG Legal Services. Communication was slow and inconsistent, which made an already stressful situation even worse. I often had to chase for updates, and when I did get responses, they weren’t always clear or helpful.
I also felt that my case wasn’t given the attention or urgency it deserved. The service came across as quite impersonal, and I didn’t feel properly supported or guided through the process.

I do not usually leave reviews or complaints, which should show how serious this situation has become. However, after my experience with DLG Legal Services, I feel compelled to warn others and formally express how unacceptable their handling of my case has been.

At 18 years old, I was involved in a road traffic collision caused by a drunk driver while returning home from a night shift. I suffered physical injuries, significant emotional distress, loss of my vehicle, loss of independence, and the wider impact of the incident also affected my employment. This was an extremely difficult period of my life, and I relied on DLG Legal Services to represent my interests professionally and efficiently.

Instead, the experience has been defined by delay, poor communication, and a complete lack of confidence in their ability to manage a straightforward claim.

I am now approaching 21 years old next month, meaning this matter has continued for nearly three years with no satisfactory conclusion. Over that period, my case has been transferred between three separate handlers without proper explanation or continuity. Each transfer created the impression that progress had stalled and that I had to start again.

Communication has been shockingly poor throughout. Messages sent through the online message centre have been read and then ignored for months at a time. Calls are not returned, updates are not proactively provided, and I have repeatedly been left chasing for basic information regarding my own case.

For a legal service dealing with clients who may already be suffering stress, injury, financial difficulty, or trauma following accidents, this level of service is wholly unacceptable. Clients should not be left feeling abandoned or forgotten.

My honest advice to anyone being directed towards DLG Legal Services through their insurer is to carefully consider seeking independent representation elsewhere. Had I known how poorly this would be handled, I would have chosen my own solicitors from the start.

This has been one of the most frustrating and disappointing professional services I have ever dealt with. There appears to be no urgency, no accountability, and no customer care.

If a zero-star rating were possible, that is what I would give.

If you could give nil stars I would have chosen that option, ive never dealt with such an incompetent company in all my life. Do your management, get management training on interviewing candidates. I recently interviewed here for a role with Jamila Noel & Rob Salekipour and I wanted to share feedback on the candidate experience.

Jamila Noel & Rob Salekipour – I am writing to formally share my feedback regarding my recent interview experience, and to request an apology for aspects of the process that I found unprofessional.
The interview was scheduled for a specific time, yet both of them joined approximately ten minutes late without any acknowledgement or apology. While I understand that meetings can overrun, punctuality is typically expected of candidates. The absence of any recognition of the delay felt discourteous and set an uncomfortable tone from the outset.
During the interview, I was asked whether I had applied directly or had been headhunted — information that would have been available at application stage. This question was revisited in a way that felt unnecessary and unclear in purpose. Additionally, there was significant focus on personal circumstances that did not appear clearly relevant to the role. While I appreciate that interviews should explore motivation and suitability, this line of questioning felt intrusive rather than constructive.
I was also informed in feedback that it was “unprofessional” for me to mention my current company. However, it was referenced multiple times during the interview and I was prompted on that topic. Being criticised for responding to a line of questioning initiated by the interviewers felt inconsistent and unfair.
Furthermore, I was told that I would receive an outcome within two weeks, yet I was informed of the decision within a few hours. While a prompt response is appreciated, this contradicted what was communicated and contributed to an overall sense of disorganisation.
To be clear, this feedback relates specifically to the interview structure and conduct, not the organisation as a whole. I left the process feeling disappointed — not only by the outcome, but by the professionalism of the experience itself.
Given the above, I believe an acknowledgement and apology for the delay and elements of the interview conduct would be appropriate.
I hope this feedback is taken constructively to improve the candidate experience moving forward.

I never thought I’d be writing a dental review like this after being with the same practice for many years with “Dentist” Samiyah Kalam, but here we are both my patience and my tooth seem to have reached their limit at the same time.

I went in with severe tooth pain expecting answers, a plan, and ideally the promise that I could stop thinking about my mouth for five minutes. I was told I needed a root canal because the tooth was in poor condition, which I accepted at that point I wasn’t emotionally attached anymore.

What I wasn’t prepared for was the financial and informational plot twist that followed.
After already paying a consultation fee of £27, I was quoted £312 for a root canal without a crown. Under NHS banding, Band 2 (around £75) typically covers root canal treatment, and Band 3 (around £332) covers root canal plus crown. So I somehow ended up being offered the “full Band 3 experience” minus one of the main features like booking a holiday package and finding out the hotel is optional.

To make things more reassuring, I was also told there is no guarantee the root canal will work and the tooth may still need to be removed afterwards anyway. So essentially: pay a significant amount for a procedure that might be a farewell tour rather than a long-term solution.

Understandably, I hesitated. At that point I was also told that if I didn’t proceed immediately, I would no longer be seen for that tooth, which added a certain sense of urgency I wasn’t emotionally or financially prepared for. She also told me I was just wasted 30mins of her time and look at me unpleasantly.

What made the experience most frustrating wasn’t just the pain or the cost, but the lack of clear explanation. Everything felt rushed and difficult to follow at a time when I really needed clarity rather than a pop quiz in dental economics.

I left feeling like I’d attended a medical appointment, a financial negotiation, and a choose your own adventure book where every ending involves losing the tooth anyway.

After years of loyalty, I expected clear communication and reassurance. Instead, I left with tooth pain, confusion, and the growing suspicion that my mouth and my bank account are no longer on speaking terms.

After having several teeth removed, I’m unfortunately returning to Abbey Dental for another appointment, even though I had been trying to avoid further treatment there and keep my remaining teeth. If you’ve had a similar experience, it may be worth joining a waitlist for another dentist before it’s too late. And if you are thinking of joining be prepared.

Faced with an obvious discrepancy between the information provided and reality, the response I received was defensive, unprofessional, and delivered in an inappropriate tone, including the repeated use of all caps and reproaches directed at the customer. At no point was there any genuine willingness to verify the information or offer an effective solution; instead, there was a confrontational attitude unbecoming of a customer-oriented service.

It should be noted that the only positive aspect was the driver's conduct, who was courteous and professional during the delivery. However, this does not compensate for the previous shortcomings in management and, especially, in the customer service received.

In short, I believe that Cafler urgently needs to review both its communication protocols and the training of its customer service staff, as the experience offered falls far short of what one would expect from a professional service.

If I could give 0 stars, I would. The car itself seemed fine at the beginning, but then, within 6 months, we had 3 different and COSTLY problems with the car. Within those 6 months, we were covered by the warranty, meaning Grant had to legally pay for the issues as they were issues that came with the car upon purchase and for those issues under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. He sold us a faulty car and claimed that it had been checked over before the sale.

We went to different and independent mechanics, and they all said that the car had barely received an inspection before sale, it was just enough to pass the MOT. When contacting Grant, not only did he tells us we had to pay to fix those things out of our own pockets as he has a small business and cannot afford to pay for these things (even though the warranty and the law says he must do so), he is currently trying to force us to pay him back for 1/3 of the problems he helped to pay for. And the cherry on top: he is threatening to take US TO COURT for something that could have been avoided if he had carried out an adequate inspection of the car.

We were met with: A flat battery which had to get completely replaced, 4 worn out break pads which were a safety issue and had to get replaced, and just last week, we had a loose piece at the front of the car; the crank pulley was loose, very worn out, and making noises when driving. The total of all of this was a whooping cost of £900, £400 of which we paid, £500 of which he is asking us to pay half of, as if he wasn't legally required to pay the £500 anyway.

Grant doesn't operate on a good faith basis, he wants to sell you a car full of problems and blame it on you when you try to take it up with him. He is nice and kind at the beginning to make you feel bad for trying to make him pay for the car, with the excuse that he is a "small business", even though he is legally required to pay. I really hate leaving negative reviews, and avoid them when I can, but when it comes to something as serious and as expensive as a car, this is no longer a joking matter. And I see I am not alone in this given I have seen plently of reviews pointing to the same issue.

Avoid this dealership if you can, and hold Grant to account where he is trying to avoid liability for the faulty products he is selling.

Gosh, I almost never write bad reviews, but I had such a disappointing experience here that I felt compelled to. I dined in on May 14th with a group of six, so we were able to try a good portion of the menu.

The lamb with cime de rapa was nicely cooked, but almost everything else our table received was cooked improperly, which was so strange. The turbot and rabbit saddle were absolutely hammered: chewy and tough to eat. But at least they were edible.

Three people in our party ordered short rib with saffron risotto, and what came was an undercooked short rib mostly comprised of un-rendered fat, accompanied by an undercooked (i.e. hard-in-the-centre) risotto. Imagine basically being served a plate of chewy, uncooked, beef fat. I really don't like to write bad reviews, but god, I'm still getting nauseous two days later thinking about what was placed in front of me.

When we flagged to the waitstaff that the "beef" (again, it was mostly un-rendered fat) was basically inedible, they were apologetic and assured us that if we had flagged it sooner they would have swapped it for something else for us, but the thing was that nobody came by our table (to check on us, refill drinks, anything!) after they dropped the food at the table.

Listen, I get that restaurants have bad days, and a restaurant that comes up with a daily menu is bound to have some misses, but charging upwards of thirty pounds per (small) entree when the proteins are so abysmally prepared is a bit outrageous, you guys.

I booked a full service and MOT for my BMW 1 Series through ClickMechanic because of the assurances on their website about vetted mechanics and not needing to “worry about a thing”.

Unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite - leading to a great deal of stress, a damaged car, court cases and police reports.

The mechanic assigned to me retained my car for several weeks with very little communication and repeatedly missed agreed return dates. When the car was eventually returned, it had sustained damage to the front bumper, wheel arch and headlamp units which was not present when the vehicle was collected. I also discovered that approximately 800 miles had been added to the odometer while the car was in the mechanic’s possession, without my permission. The police later tracked the number plate and informed me that the car had been spotted driving in many locations far away from where the mechanic was based.

To make matters worse, the invoice for the work referenced a limited company that had already been dissolved many months before the booking. Despite repeated requests, I was never provided with clear insurance details.

I ultimately had to:
* pursue a chargeback through Amex
* report the matter to Hertfordshire Constabulary
* issue a Letter Before Action
* begin Small Claims Court proceedings to recover the cost of repairing the damage, which I wasn’t able to do

ClickMechanic did remove the mechanic from the platform after I raised concerns, but ultimately took the position that they are only an introductory marketplace and accepted no liability for what happened.

I appreciate that marketplaces cannot control every individual mechanic, but I relied heavily on the company’s marketing around vetting, trust and customer protection when deciding to hand over my vehicle.

I’m left with a damaged car and a court process which has yielded no results. Even the police have been unable to track down this ‘vetted’ mechanic. He has disappeared off the surface of the earth - and didn’t live at the address supplied to ClickMechanic.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others against using this platform. Do not give over your car to a mechanic through this platform, as ClickMechanic will accept absolutely no responsibility if something goes wrong.

We used ClickMechanic for a pre-purchase inspection before buying a van and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience.

The report marked key areas such as “body damage” and “past repairs” as “not fitted”, and stated that major components (including tyres and overall condition) were in working order. Based on this, we proceeded with the purchase.

Within a month, we discovered significant issues that were not identified in the inspection, including a cut in the bodywork, evidence of previous sealing, water ingress, and early rust. A local garage confirmed these issues and quoted over £1,000 just for initial repair work, with more extensive repairs likely needed.

Shortly after purchase, one of the tyres also blew out while driving, which could easily have led to a serious accident. The inspection had not flagged any concerns with the tyres.

When we raised this with ClickMechanic, they declined responsibility, stating they are only a marketplace connecting customers with mechanics.

We appreciate that inspections have limitations, but in this case the issues appear to have been visible and material, and we would have expected them to be flagged or at least noted in the report.

We will now be escalating this via Citizens Advice and Trading Standards.

Overall, the inspection gave us a false sense of confidence and we would advise others to proceed with caution.

It’s been a few months as I was too heartbroken to write about this and re-live the story again.

I brought my 15-year-old cat, Theresa, to Leyton Midland Vets on 31/10/2025 because she had been vomiting daily and was clearly unwell. Despite this, and despite a suspected diagnosis of chronic kidney disease noted by the vet, she was given multiple vaccinations, a deworming tablet, and parasite treatment during the same visit without any prior blood or urine testing.

Just days later, on 03/11/2025, her condition worsened dramatically. She developed severe breathing difficulties, something she had never experienced before. After rushing her back in, tests revealed serious multi-organ issues, including kidney, liver, and pancreatic complications, as well as fluid around her lungs. She was discharged later that day still struggling to breathe, and heartbreakingly passed away that same evening in a very painful and traumatic way.

I truly believe that administering her multiple treatments while she was already unwell placed severe strain on her body and contributed to her rapid decline. Theresa was a deeply loved member of my family, and losing her in this way has been really devastating for all of us.

I hope this review encourages reflection and change, so that no other pet or owner has to go through something like this again.

I am absolutely heartbroken and deeply disappointed with the care we received. I cannot understand why a vaccination was given when my cat was already showing signs of illness. I feel that this decision showed a serious lack of clinical judgment and have contributed to her death.

This has been an incredibly distressing experience for me and my family  and we are still grieving the loss of my cat. Based on what happened, I would not recommend this practice, as I no longer have confidence in the standard of care provided.

I hope the practice reflects seriously on this situation to prevent other pet owners from going through the same painful experience .
