They keep deleting my review as they don’t want the truth to come out:
As someone who has worked in respected nurseries including Northbridge House and Windmill Montessori, I can honestly say my experience at Little Sweethearts was deeply disappointing and concerning.
On the surface, the nursery presents itself as warm, caring, and professional, but behind closed doors the reality felt very different. There was a strong culture of favouritism amongst staff, very little organisation, and an atmosphere where employees felt unable to speak openly. Staff were actively discouraged from speaking freely with parents, which created the impression that appearance mattered more than honesty and transparency.
One of the most upsetting things I witnessed was the way some SEN children appeared to be treated differently. During visits from prospective parents, SEN children were often kept away from the main areas, which gave the impression the nursery was trying to present a polished image rather than an honest one. In my opinion, this was unfair and isolating for those children.
I also found it concerning that certain staff members were discouraged from speaking to parents because management believed foreign accents would “put parents off.” I found this extremely uncomfortable and inappropriate in such a diverse childcare environment.
The nursery advertises itself as very outdoors-focused, but in reality children were not consistently taken outside every day despite what parents may believe.
In the baby room upstairs, I was also shocked by the unprofessional attitude shown by certain staff members. Hearing babies described as “disgusting” for normal things such as mucus, snot, or dirty nappies was upsetting and completely unacceptable in a childcare setting.
Another major concern was the reluctance to raise possible signs of neglect or wellbeing concerns with parents because staff feared causing offence. In childcare, safeguarding and honesty should always come before protecting the nursery’s image.
Overall, my experience was that the nursery cared more about maintaining appearances than providing a genuinely supportive, inclusive, and transparent environment for children and staff. Parents deserve honesty, professionalism, and proper care for every child, including SEN children, and sadly I did not feel that standard was being met

I was advised by my midwives to book a reflexology appointment, as at 36 weeks my baby was breech, and we were running out of time to turn him back around. Reflexology is recommended by the NHS as a complementary therapy to turn breech babies, so I booked an appointment.

When I arrived, I was shown to a room and the technician started unwrapping sterilised needles for acupuncture. I clarified I had booked reflexology and she said that acupuncture is what works, and reflexology doesn't work.

Acupuncture is also more expensive than reflexology, so she had not only changed my appoinment without telling me, she had changed it to a more expensive one.

ZERO star. Please read the negative’s reviews and save your hard earned money. The is company is a scam. I ordered the Noami wig. It came with barely any hair at the top. The little hair there was, were short strands. I posted on the IG and sent pictures. Mind you this was a week after receiving the wig. I was told to share how I wash the wig or the brush. I immediately told them I hadn’t worn it at that time. I then worn it once but the lace was too visible to keep. I went to the store and the manager told me I needed to part the hair right in a way that it will cover the lace👀. She also told me I can’t get an exchange but only a refund because I had given them one star On Trustpilot. I told her I stand by my review and I want a refund.
Now the issue with the Noami wig I got was not just the lack of hair or balding, the hair was also shedding when I ran my fingers through and the only time I wore it, it matted at the back. All the qualities they claim on the product page are non existent. They are buying hair on Aliexpress and selling it to us 100s of pounds.

Bought The TAYLOR Deep Wave Glueless HD Lace Front Wig – Pre-Plucked Virgin Brazilian (24’ Frontal Wig) [order #40066] for £320 after an albeit generous 10% off first order.

Arrived next day through DHL in a premium-looking box including several free gifts such as melt bands & a bonnet, which also looked very promising on first glance.

However, a strong fish smell was noticeable upon opening the box before even opening any of the packaging inside. I’ve been told by a few trained hair stylists I know that fish smells indicate very low quality hair (usually “waste hair” sourced from salon floors, combs and sewers) washed in acid baths to strip its cuticles. The knots weren’t pre-bleached and the wig is neither glueless nor ready for immediate installation as described on their website.

This is NOT expected from a vendor pricing their wigs so high… I’ve seen better on TikTok shop for £100!!!!!

These 5 star reviews are clearly fake/bought since every other one in between them is a review with the exact same problems I’ve faced here. I’ve also looked up the celebrities they proudly display on their homepage - not a single one I can find mentioning this store publicly.

Low quality products, false advertising and astroturfing (fake reviews). These are the kind of people who keep jobs at Trading Standards secure and well paid.

I was expecting this hair to be high quality given the price, but unfortunately that hasn’t been my experience. I’ve followed all the recommended care instructions, and look after my hair yet the quality has been very disappointing. I’ve straightened it twice, and each time it turns frizzy. Even when worn curly, the frizz is still very noticeable.

In addition, the shedding and tangling has been excessive, honestly comparable to lower-grade hair you might find on AliExpress, which is unacceptable at this price point. It makes the hair difficult to manage and significantly affects its overall appearance and longevity.

I’m really unhappy with this purchase and quite shocked at the quality. My expectations were high, especially after seeing consistently positive reviews on TikTok and Instagram, along with videos from customers who seemed very satisfied. However, the reality hasn’t matched what was presented.

Sadly, I don’t think I’ll be purchasing ever again.

I had a really upsetting and humiliating experience at Madison, One New Change, St Paul’s.

Yesterday evening, my friend and I went there for cocktails. At the entrance, security asked only us to show ID. I explained that I had a passport copy on my phone and that there was no clear information saying a physical ID was mandatory. I understand venues have ID policies, but the way we were treated was completely unacceptable.

When I asked why we were being asked and not others, the security guard said other people had restaurant reservations. I then said I could book a table, and he replied that even if I booked, he still would not allow me in. He also said that even if I came back tomorrow, he would be there and would not let me in.

His attitude felt like, “do whatever you want, I still won’t let you in.” He kept telling us to “go, please go” in front of everyone, which felt extremely embarrassing and intimidating. I honestly felt like I was being pushed away and humiliated publicly, rather than being treated like a paying customer.

I am 26 and my friends are above 24, so this was not about being underage. I have been to many restaurants, bars, clubs, and pubs, and I have never been spoken to like this just because I did not have a physical ID with me.

What made it worse was that I contacted Madison afterwards. I was told the message would be passed to reception and that someone would call me back, but nobody did. For such a well-known venue, the lack of care and follow-up is really disappointing.

The way the situation was handled made me feel singled out, uncomfortable, and humiliated. I cannot comment on the intention, but I do believe the incident should be reviewed properly and it completely ruined our evening.

I fully respect ID checks and venue policies, but customers should be treated with respect and dignity. This was a horrible experience, and based on how we were treated by security and the lack of response from management, I would not recommend Madison.👎

A bookshop should open minds. This one felt designed to close them.

Walked in recently and noticed a large display of books on a contested geopolitical conflict (a dedicated stand plus promotion right by the till).

I asked the staff member directly: 'You're promoting and displaying only one side of a nuanced story that has two sides. Don't you think that's politically biased and not showing the full picture?' Their reply was instant & blunt: 'Yeah, that's the point.'

That stopped me.

This shop has made a deliberate choice to prominently platform many books representing one political perspective on one deeply contested conflict ... and their staff confirmed it proudly.

I'd ask: does the owner apply this same curatorial approach to every other geopolitical conflict in the world? Because the world is full of them. The answer, judging by the shelves, is no. That's not a curatorial decision. That's a double standard. And by the seller's own cheerful admission, it's intentional.

I question the ethics behind that choice entirely.

I left uncomfortable & genuinely concerned that deliberately one-sided material, proudly presented as such rather than as one perspective among many, risks fostering hostility toward a specific ethnic & religious community.

One star: not for the politics. For the intellectual dishonesty.

I booked online music lessons for both of my children after speaking with someone on the phone who explained the pricing. I thought the cost sounded reasonable and agreed to proceed.

After a few sessions, I suddenly received an invoice that was almost double the amount I had originally been told. When I queried this, I was informed that the lower price only applied if lessons were booked in bulk. This was never explained to me at the time of booking. What made it even more confusing was that the first two invoices matched the original agreed amount, so I do not understand why the pricing then suddenly changed.

I emailed explaining the situation, referred back to the phone conversation, and highlighted the original invoices as evidence. Instead of resolving the matter professionally, I began receiving daily phone calls and repeated emails chasing payment.

Due to the confusion around pricing and the overall experience, I decided to withdraw both of my children from the lessons. The sessions themselves were online, and unfortunately communication was also difficult at times as the tutor spoke very little English, which made the experience even harder to manage.

I can pay the higher amount if necessary, but the issue for me is the lack of transparency and honesty from the beginning. Overall, a very disappointing experience.

In response to the owner:
I did contact you directly by email and explained the situation in detail. I also provided copies of the original invoices, which matched the price initially discussed, as well as the email correspondence relating to the booking.

Despite this, I am still receiving repeated phone calls and payment chasing emails rather than the matter being properly resolved. My issue has never been about refusing to pay, it is about the lack of clarity and consistency around the pricing from the beginning. On a separate note I also didn’t receive the key stickers which I followed up with twice at the beginning.

MuseCool is introducing a tool that listens to piano lessons and generates summaries. This is a step in the wrong direction. Music education should be human, not monitored. Turning lessons into data points risks replacing real listening with technology.

More importantly, it raises clear privacy concerns. Even with consent, the idea of being listened to and analysed during a lesson is uncomfortable. Not everything needs to be tracked to be meaningful - especially something as personal as learning music.

I would like to share my experience with the platform in a constructive and respectful way.

I have been assigned three students through the platform. In one case, there was continuity and several paid lessons, which I consider a positive outcome. In the other two cases, the students did not continue, which is something that can happen for many different reasons and is not always within the teacher’s control.

What I find concerning is the feeling of being evaluated in a way that is not entirely transparent, and at times, indirectly held responsible for the lack of continuity. As a teacher, this creates unnecessary pressure and uncertainty.

Additionally, I have received communications that I perceived as somewhat threatening, suggesting that my account could be removed. This is particularly discouraging given that I am actively investing time in improving my profile, updating materials, and building a strong presence on the platform.

Overall, this experience has been disheartening and has led me to question whether this is a supportive and secure environment in which to develop my work as a teacher.

I would sincerely encourage the platform to review its evaluation process and ensure that it is fair, balanced, and respectful of teachers’ efforts.

Great broadband… until something goes wrong

For nearly two years, Hyperoptic was flawless. Fast, reliable, no complaints—an easy 5 stars.

Then the fibre line was damaged by another provider.

To be clear, I don’t blame Hyperoptic for the damage itself. That’s outside their control. But what is in their control is how they respond—and this is where things fall apart completely.

Frontline support is genuinely excellent: polite, responsive, and clearly trying to help. The problem is they’re totally disconnected from the teams who actually fix issues. They can’t speak to them, can’t give real updates, and can’t take ownership. It’s a broken system.

Timeline:

Sunday: Outage reported
Monday: Engineer confirms cable is beyond repair and needs a two-person team
Tuesday–Friday: Daily calls, same script—“I’ll escalate this.” No updates, no ownership, no progress
Saturday: Unable to even get through—stuck in a looped “we’re busy” message for 45 minutes before giving up

No communication. No urgency. No confirmed fix. Just silence.

What’s especially frustrating is that this exact cable was damaged a few months ago—and it was fixed quickly then. So it’s clearly possible.

We’re now still without internet, over £100 out of pocket on mobile data, and no resolution in sight.

So while the product itself is excellent, the service when things go wrong is not. And that’s what really matters.

Sorry Hyperoptic—but this experience has completely changed my view.

The scheduling model is made by someone who doesn't understand the basics of real life. All appointments are limited to weekday daytime windows, as if customers have nothing else to do. Is it expected that I'll take a day off to sit at home waiting for a vague 4-hour slot? It's not a minor inconvenience; it’s a real financial cost. There is no technical limitation here. This is simply a management decision that ignores how people actually live and work. This is absolutely ridiculous.

This isn’t a premium fibre service, it’s an unreliable system with a management problem at its core. If your time actually matters, think twice.

Dogs Welcome, Children Not: A Masterclass in Inconsistency and Inhospitality

I rarely feel the need to write a scathing review, but our recent experience here was so profoundly poorly managed that I feel obligated to warn other families. Despite booking a private room in advance and explicitly notifying the restaurant that we would have three children—including an infant under the age of two—the management seemed determined to make our evening as difficult as possible.

The "No Outside Food" Absurdity

The most egregious part of the night involved our youngest. We brought a small container of soft, safe foods (a banana, a whole avocado, and strawberries) specifically because we knew our under-two needed soft options.

The Policy: Management confiscated the child’s food, claiming it violated policy.

The Alternative: They insisted he order from the "Children’s Menu," yet they could not guarantee any salt-free options.

The Result: The menu had zero appropriate soft foods for a baby his age. After being forced to try their options, our child ended up vomiting. We ultimately had to leave mid-meal to find a restaurant that would actually allow us to feed our baby.

Prams vs. Pups

The "family-friendly" facade continued to crumble with the pram policy. We were told prams were strictly prohibited in the dining area and had to be stored downstairs. This became a logistical nightmare when the baby fell asleep.

The kicker? This policy is applied with zero consistency. A couple seated right behind us was permitted to have their pram at the table. Furthermore, we witnessed multiple dogs being welcomed into the restaurant and treated with significantly more warmth and flexibility than our children.

Bizarre Service & Stuffy Logic

When we tried to simplify things by ordering a side of plain white rice for the kids, we were told it was impossible—it had to have vinegar. In a sushi restaurant, where rice is the foundational ingredient, the claim that they cannot provide a bowl of plain boiled rice is lazy and nonsensical.

The "logic" extended to the door staff as well. We witnessed a gentleman’s friend being denied entry for wearing shorts, despite the fact that his companion was already seated inside wearing the exact same matching shorts. It felt less like a "standard" and more like a series of arbitrary hurdles.

The Bottom Line

For the price point, the food is strictly average. There are at least three other restaurants in the immediate vicinity serving similar cuisine with far more professional management and better value.

The only saving grace: Our waiter in the private room was lovely and did his best with the hand he was dealt. However, his service couldn't mask the toxic and discriminatory management style.

Avoid this place if you have children. Apparently, you’re better off bringing a dog

Very disappointed！！Appointments are only available once every two weeks, and even after finally securing one, the shopping time is heavily restricted. Today London traffic was terrible and there was also a Tube strike. Because this was my first time visiting the store, I genuinely hoped for a good shopping experience. I wasn’t even looking for anything rare or highly specific. I simply wanted to choose a suitable long-sleeve or short-sleeve shirt.

When I realised I might be slightly late, I even called the store seriously and politely in advance. However, once I arrived, I personally witnessed another male customer ahead of me having his service cut short early simply because he “walked around the first floor.” I overheard the conversation clearly, and the customer never said he no longer needed service, nor had his appointment time ended. Yet the staff unilaterally terminated his appointment early.

Unsurprisingly, when it was my turn upstairs, I also received terrible service. I basically made the trip for nothing. The store had almost no clothing available except a few off-season down jackets on display. I repeatedly said I only wanted to see long-sleeve or short-sleeve shirts, and somehow they could not provide a single item to try or even browse properly. The attitude was also extremely cold and dismissive.

The entire appointment system felt pointless. The store was full of people, and the staff all looked “busy,” but honestly it was unclear what they were actually doing. Customers could barely receive basic service, yet there were endless rules imposed on them (for example, being restricted to staying only on the second floor during service).

I genuinely do not understand where this sense of superiority comes from. Whether it is selective treatment based on appearance or a discriminatory attitude toward certain customers, this is a very serious issue. This is not the brand image an international luxury brand should present. I have experienced much better service at many other brands, both more expensive and less expensive than Chrome Hearts.

Especially the female sales associate working today, her attitude was extremely unfriendly and dismissive throughout the interaction, which made the entire experience even more uncomfortable.

Not a very nice welcoming experience for a brand with such a long and amazing history.

I recently visited Duck & Waffle with high expectations given the pricing and reputation, but unfortunately the overall experience was disappointing.

The ambience lacked the atmosphere you would expect from a restaurant charging near fine-dining or Michelin-level prices. While the location and views are impressive, the dining experience itself felt closer to standard pub food rather than a premium restaurant experience.

The food presentation was underwhelming, and the main course lacked freshness and quality. The duck leg was extremely dry and tasted as though it had been sitting for some time rather than freshly prepared. The waffle itself was also disappointing in texture and flavour.

Really disappointing and upsetting experience at Duck & Waffle. This was only our second time visiting London, and after struggling to find somewhere serving food late at night, we were excited to finally find what we thought was simply a restaurant open late.
I was in heels, my husband was dressed nicely, and although we didn’t even know there was a dress code, we were clearly dressed appropriately for dinner. We had no idea a restaurant would have bouncers at the door or that getting in for dinner could even be an issue.
What made the experience so upsetting was how we were treated. The first bouncer had us wait in line for around 15 minutes, only for the second bouncer to take one look at us and arrogantly say, “Not today,” before turning us away without any explanation.
What made it feel even worse was that we were the only Latinos standing at the door, and we watched person after person get let in—many without reservations—while we were turned away immediately. I can’t say what their reasoning was, but in that moment it absolutely felt discriminatory, humiliating, and deeply upsetting.
After walking all the way there, waiting in line, and genuinely just looking for a late-night meal, being dismissed like that with no explanation was incredibly frustrating. Nowhere on their website does it make it clear that people coming for dinner can simply be turned away at the door.
This left a really bad impression of what should have been a special night in London. We left feeling embarrassed, confused, and honestly hurt. Based on our experience, I’d avoid going.

I really wanted to like this place, but unfortunately my experience fell short both in quality and overall service.

My gel manicure didn’t last. Multiple nails started peeling within a couple of days, and had lifted or come off. I was later told that an e-file is 100% necessary to prevent this, but that isn’t true and hasn’t been my experience at other salons in London (e.g. Shoreditch Nails, Townhouse) or back home in Canada, where gel manicures have lasted much longer without issue.

More concerning, though, was the atmosphere during the appointment. The technician seemed visibly frustrated at times—sighing when I accidentally smudged a nail or when I asked about changing my French tip colour. It made me feel quite anxious and uncomfortable, to the point where I didn’t feel at ease communicating what I wanted and just wanted the appointment to be over.

What stood out even more was another client sitting beside me who appeared to be experiencing similar treatment. She became so upset that she started crying and asked not to be spoken to that way. While the tone improved after that, it shouldn’t have gotten to that point for either of us.

To the salon’s credit, a repair/discount was offered. However, given both the poor longevity of the manicure and the overall experience, I didn’t feel comfortable returning.

There is a nice, busy atmosphere in the salon, which suggests it’s popular. But for me, getting my nails done should feel relaxing, and unfortunately this wasn’t that experience.

For that price point, go elsewhere that are cleaner, friendlier, and more professional IMO.

I've had a really poor customer service experience after a sofabed I bought online was delivered with many defects (a badly chipped plinth, as well nicks, cuts and scuffs on the fabric in four places).

I reported the defects immediately to both the delivery men and sent photos to Darlings directly. It was very clear that the nicks and cuts couldn't be brushed out but they insisted that they send a technician who would be able to brush them out. That entailed the inconvenience of setting aside a whole day as they won't book a specific time slot. When I complained about the inconvenience, they said they could send a regular delivery man with a brush, such was their dismissive attitude to the damage - in fact as time went on I have been made to feel like I'm a nuisance.

The technician came and reported that none of the fabric damage could be made good (as was obvious all along). She also stated that in-situ reupholstering would be inappropriate as the replacement fabric (both arms and the entire 2m back) would be folded in transit which would certainly leave a permanent mark to the nap of the velvet. She said she had written that in her report. Despite this report, Darlings emailed to say that they were pleased the marks had "improved" (they are all still there), but they will offer in situ re-upholstery. Alternatively I could keep the sofa and they would offer a £120 discount (a tiny fraction of the cost and a fraction of what it would cost them to reupholster). The discount was insulting - a reputable firm should be offering that and fixing the problem, given how many hours of back and forth with their customer service team I've had to endure. I pushed back, and they came back with a workshop based reupholstering (which will entail giving up more time to be around for collection and delivery windows).

They then reneged on that offer. Insisting my only option was an in situ reupholstering. I said OK. Weeks went by without word. I have been left with a damaged sofa for nearly three months now. They contacted me to say that I would need to be around to take delivery of the fabric, I would then need to store it until they could arrange an upholsterer to visit. I had already made it clear that the upholsterer should arrive with the fabric and I shouldn't be inconvenienced like that and they had agreed, but have reneged again. I pointed this out in an email (we are at 45 emails now) and they ignored me.

I don't know whether the customer service team are liars or whether they are just disorganised and incompetent. Regardless, their customer service is appalling. Given the compensation they offered was so low - so much lower than the cost of new fabric and an upholsterer's time - I suspect that they are hoping I will just give up and go away.

Buy British? Don't bother. A predatory and frustrating experience. Rating: 1 / 5

The UK Brand Myth: I paid a significant premium for these locks because I wanted to support a UK business and have the peace of mind of London-based support. It was a massive mistake. Simpled is a corporate facade operating out of a WeWork address, selling fragile hardware with a support system designed to stall and frustrate.

Pricing Chaos: There is zero consistency in their pricing. They list these locks at £169 on their website, sometimes discounted to £99, while charging £139 on Amazon. It is a blatant attempt to see how much they can squeeze out of you.

The Hardware Saga: I ordered three units initially. One arrived with a broken front panel. Despite the heavy price tag, this isn't some bespoke system. The locks run entirely on a basic, third-party app (TTLock). Worse yet, the core biometric feature is practically useless; the fingerprint sensor is so unreliable that the lock mostly wouldn't open even after 8 to 10 attempts. The replacement I eventually received for the broken unit appeared to be a used customer return and was just as defective.

The Most Ridiculous Part: When I had to replace another faulty component, the shipping took a full week. To make matters worse, they had the audacity to blame me for a part that broke while I was simply trying to fix their defective hardware. They then tried to charge me an extra £33 for the replacement part. I was only in that position because their original product was faulty, yet they tried to turn it into a profit-making opportunity.

The Support Nightmare: They boast about UK resident support, yet it routinely took them 24 hours or more to reply to a basic email. I spent a week in an exhausting loop of stalling tactics. Even after management admitted they got many things wrong, they suggested a resolution with an offer I didn't even ask for. Given the days of physical labor and the sheer administrative hassle they caused, the offer was quite frankly insulting anyway!

The Truth: I have since ripped these out and replaced them with alternative locks that cost only £40. To be honest, the £40 replacements are far superior in every way. The biometrics work instantly and the build quality puts Simpled to shame.

The Verdict: Save your money, your time, and your doors. You can buy a better product for £40 elsewhere and avoid the headache of a company that cares more about its image than its customers.

It is up to you to make your own mind up, but I have done the legwork so you don't have to.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wanted to share my experience as a prospective buyer looking at a parcel of land marketed through Barney Estates. After posting my first review, I received a formal letter from RLL Legal (acting for Barney Estates) asking me to remove it within hours. That experience has shaped how much weight I personally place on the overall star rating here. This is, of course, my personal opinion based on my own interaction with the company and their solicitor.

I did not complete the purchase, but I reviewed the documents carefully. This is not legal advice; it is simply my personal perspective.

Here are the points that stood out to me:

1. The seller’s position was different from what I expected

When I reviewed the documents provided, I learned that the seller had not yet completed their own purchase of the land. They were in the process of buying it under a “Top Contract”.

Amiee Bryett informed me:

I would have to complete within 28 days
The seller would have 16 weeks to complete

This was unfamiliar to me, and I personally found it worrying and more high risk than the land purchases I have explored before. I was left under the impression that my access to the land I was buying, could be in jeopardy, if the seller failed to complete on their own purchase of the land. I felt that this would leave me in a vulnerable position if my purchase was to be completed months before that of the seller.

2. The contract pack felt very seller favourable

The documents included limited scope for enquiries, the buyer being deemed to have full knowledge of title, minimal warranties, and a limited title guarantee. I had not encountered such terms before and was not happy with them.

3. The TP1 contained to me unexpected restrictions

The draft TP1 included:
-No express rights of access over retained land
-Rights reserved to the seller
-Obligations to contribute to maintenance of certain areas on retained land

This made me feel that the land might be more limited in use than I had thought.

4. The overage clause felt unusually long and complex

The overage clause in the draft documents lasted for 80 years and included various triggers and valuation mechanisms that I have never seen in an overage clause before. Overage clauses are not uncommon in some transactions, but the length and structure of this one felt more complex than I was happy with. Even after proposed amendments, I kept discovering more things about it that I found problematic. This made me worried that future fees and associated charges could become a financial burden and have an impact on the sale of the land in the future.

5. I found the seller’s identity surprising

When checking with Companies House the name on the Memorandum of Sale, I found a HR company based in Rotherham. It made me wonder why a HR firm was flipping farmland in Essex. There are probably several good reasons for it, but I am not familiar enough with the industry to comprehend these.

This is not a criticism - just an honest reflection of my experience.

6. The fees were higher than I expected

The documents listed several fees payable by the buyer, including:

a buyer’s premium (£8,000.00)
a contract fee (£6,000.00)
the seller’s legal fees (£3,250.00)

Auction fees vary widely, but these were higher than what I have personally come across. I had, for example, not heard of a buyer's premium before. There were additional fees in the contract and on the TP1 that I would have been responsible for should I have signed the contract and/or completed the purchase.

7. The auctioneer acts for the seller

The documents made clear that the auctioneer acts for the seller, not the buyer. This is standard in auctions, but it is worth being aware of. Amiee was very polite and made me almost forget this. After paying a deposit (25.5k) to receive the legal pack, the legally binding Memorandum of Sale was emailed to be signed. I think it is important not to forget to always consult a solicitor before signing any paperwork. Barney Estates did not tell me to seek legal advice.

TLDR: NEVER use this company!!! They won’t deliver your order and you have to chase them to get a response. The one star is only because I can’t give zero.

Buckle up while I tell you about the worst company I’ve ever had to deal with. In late January I reached out to Stitch99 hoping to buy a set of custom t-shirts for my best friend’s hen. Leo then Isaac eagerly reached out claiming they would be able to do this, even offering to price match other quotes I received. Little did I know I was about to be falsely promised things they couldn’t deliver on. For the first two weeks Isaac was very responsive and helpful, he sent me different options of what they could create. Then came time for payment, and this is when it took a steep turn downhill. After providing payment, Isaac was nowhere to be found. I constantly had to follow up with him to receive an update on the order and design. On February 17, given the lack of communication,  I provided a deadline of March 6 for the t-shirts to be delivered. I was told payment was received and they’d send the design for sign off by EOD. Two days later, on February 19, I received the design and the same day I sent my comments. When I hadn’t heard from them for five days, on February 24, I followed up and asked if they’d make the deadline. Another two days go by and after following up again, on February 26, they responded and said they’d make the deadline. The following day, February 27, given the lack of communication I asked for a refund. The same day Isaac said they could offer a partial refund but “rest assured we’ll meet your deadline.” March 6 came and went and I had no t-shirts. Even more concerning, I also had no communication from Isaac saying he wouldn’t make the deadline or giving me any type of update. No, I wouldn’t hear from Isaac until a week after I was supposed to receive my order.

Then came trying to get a refund from Stitch 99. Isaac claimed he could only give a partial refund despite giving me nothing of what I ordered except the artwork. I spent four days going back and forth with Isaac, with me offering to only receive a refund for the t-shirts portion of the order and forfeiting the payment for the artwork. After agreeing, Isaac told me that I was “misleading” and “inconsiderate” of his services despite the weeks of non communication and not being able to deliver my order. Also, he said that the 5-7 working day delivery he quoted initially wasn’t a guarantee. Confusing to me that it was mentioned after the fact and not communicated before they took the payment, but alas. While I will fully acknowledge that I had very specific designs for this order, if you can’t deliver something then say that upfront. Don’t keep claiming that you can meet certain standards and a deadline, when you clearly cannot.

Next up was Isaac said my refund would be processed in five days. Nope, it took a whole four weeks and constant follow ups from me. Not surprising at this point!

After fourth months of dealing with Stitch99 I’m happy to never have to do it again. I recommend anyone considering this company to find truly ANYONE ELSE. I’d even do it yourself before trusting this company. There are companies who know how to be professional and have great customer service, Stitch99 is not one of them.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m very disappointed with the customer service at Invisiblebraces4U Islington.

Before payment, the communication was much more proactive, but once I had paid for the braces, it became very difficult to get timely responses. I was asked to order additional braces, which I have now been waiting around four weeks for, and there still seems to be no clear update on where they are or when I will receive them.

Communication via WhatsApp has been particularly poor, with messages often going unanswered for days. When I asked how to raise a complaint, I was simply given an email address rather than any meaningful support or attempt to resolve the issue.

They are not the cheapest provider, and even if they were, the level of aftercare and customer service would still be disappointing. They appear to be very good at promoting themselves on social media, but my experience of their customer care has been well below par.

Based on my experience, I would recommend researching other Invisalign or clear aligner providers before choosing Invisiblebraces4U Islington.

My experience with this clinic has been extremely disappointing, mainly due to the lack of communication and organisation. The reception team rarely seems to know what is going on, and every time you contact them, you end up back at square one repeating yourself. Calls are rarely followed up, appointments are difficult to get, and when you finally do get one, everything feels rushed with very little explanation or clarity.

I have spent months going back and forth trying to get simple issues resolved. There is constant misinformation, poor communication between staff, and no proper follow-through. Even when I was finally given a “resolution” after repeatedly chasing things up, it still was not actually resolved. I was promised reimbursement within 4–5 working days, which never happened, and the specific agent I was told to contact for future support never replied to me. So even the outcome of the complaint led to another complaint.

What makes it even more frustrating is that there is no way to properly escalate concerns. You are constantly told to “put in a complaint,” but complaints are never followed up. It genuinely feels like you are going around in circles with no accountability.

For a company that promotes itself as the number one Invisalign provider, the customer service is shockingly poor. It feels like the focus is on taking on more and more clients rather than properly managing and supporting the customers they already have.

I would strongly recommend considering other providers, even if they are slightly more expensive. Better communication, organisation, and customer care are worth paying for.

If I could give zero stars, I would. This branch is extremely disappointing. To begin with, the customer service lacks basic communication. My initial consultation was positive, and the dentists I saw made me feel comfortable and not rushed. However, since that consultation, the experience has steadily declined.

After purchasing the Invisalign treatment, I was sent a link offering to expedite my aligners to 2 weeks instead of the 5–6 weeks initially quoted. Despite this, I waited over a month for them to arrive, with repeated updates stating they were “in transit.” When they finally arrived, I had to call the clinic myself, only to be told they had been sitting there for several days and no one had contacted me to arrange a fitting appointment. This was extremely frustrating, as had I not called, no appointment would have been arranged.

The reception staff were unhelpful and repeatedly reiterated the same points rather than attempting to resolve the issue. When I asked to speak with a manager, I was informed that they were short-staffed and that no senior staff were available.

I submitted a complaint via email after the delay, and received a response assuring me that everything was in order and simply delayed. I trusted this and left it in their hands. However, the email had no signature, which I found highly unprofessional, as I had no idea who was responding — only a generic “kind regards.”

Regarding the fitting appointment, I received multiple confirmation messages with conflicting times. I believed my appointment had been moved from 2:50pm to 3:15pm, but later received a confirmation stating 3:50pm. When I called to clarify and request an earlier time, I was told no earlier appointments were available, which made the earlier time offer unclear. When I arrived at the Islington branch at 3:45pm, I was told my appointment had been scheduled for 3:00pm. I was extremely frustrated and showed my confirmation message stating 3:50pm.

During my fitting appointment, I felt rushed and the instructions provided were unclear. The dentist mentioned “attachments” without properly explaining what they were. When I returned home and removed my aligners, I noticed small studs on my teeth and initially attempted to remove them, only then realising these were the attachments. Communication from both clinical and reception staff has been consistently poor.

I was instructed to download the Invisalign app so that my treatment coordinator could monitor my progress; however, I have not been assigned a specific coordinator, nor has this process been explained to me. When I asked questions through the app, the responses were very direct and came across as unprofessional. I was also told how to take photos for monitoring, but was not provided with the required tools or shown how to properly use the app. I don’t even have the tools they’re talking about in the app.

I now feel obligated to continue with this treatment despite being dissatisfied from the outset. After reading other reviews, I am concerned that I may not achieve the results I expected.

I also attempted to contact Dr Soumaya via Instagram regarding these issues but received no response.

Overall, this clinic appears to prioritise profit over patient care. I strongly advise others to reconsider and seek treatment elsewhere, even if it may be more expensive, as you are more likely to receive proper care.

I had a very disappointing experience with this practice. At my initial appointment, everything sounded promising—I was told I would have a dedicated contact person to guide me through my treatment and that I’d be informed about my review appointment when I reached my final aligner. Unfortunately, none of that materialised.

More than a year into treatment, I’m still having to chase them just to book appointments, which are already difficult to secure. Promised phone calls never came, and emails often go unanswered. The practice in Islington feels completely disorganised.

Even when you do manage to get an appointment, there are long waits, and on several occasions the dentists seemed unclear about the purpose of my visit. Overall, the lack of communication and coordination has been extremely frustrating.

I would not recommend this practice.

Don’t get Invisalign from Invisible Braces4U.

The customer support is honestly terrible. I finished my treatment and ordered refinements, but I’ve now been stuck wearing my last aligner for 10 weeks with no progress.

After waiting 8 weeks, I was told my new aligners had arrived — only to find out they were sent to the wrong clinic (one I’ve never even visited).

Since then, I’ve called every day for the past 6 days. Every time I’m told a manager will call me back to fix it… and no one ever does. Just the same empty promises.

I’ve paid for this treatment, but they’re not delivering or taking responsibility. It’s really hard to get in touch with them. Being left in limbo like this is unacceptable especially since I’ve paid thousands of pounds for this.

Avoid.

Communication is non-existent, it’s so hard to try and speak to someone! After paying my deposit coincidentally I started to see loads of other people’s negative reviews with this company all over social media. It’s all a marketing tactic. Spend that little extra more money at an actual dentist practice where you will get the results you want!

Really disappointing and misleading advertising from Dr Soumaya Zinet and her clinic invisible.braces4u

There’s a relentless stream of ads on Instagram pushing Invisalign for “£999,” which sounds great — until you actually go through a proper consultation and the price jumps significantly. That headline figure clearly doesn’t reflect what most people will pay.

I understand treatments vary in complexity, but advertising a price that applies to a tiny minority (if anyone at all) feels deliberately misleading. It sets false expectations just to get people through the door.

It comes across more like a marketing tactic than genuine transparency. Patients deserve clear, honest pricing upfront — not a bait-and-switch once you’re already invested in the process.

Based on this experience, I wouldn’t trust these jokers and would strongly suggest others look elsewhere.

Wouldn’t recommend them at all… my 6 month treatment got extended for another 6 months because the initial treatment plan made my teeth worse so now I’m doing another round to correct their mistake.. wouldn’t recommend them at all! Go elsewhere

I am currently undergoing Invisalign treatment and unfortunately the final stage has been very poorly managed.

There have been multiple delays, including issues with my final scan which I was only informed about after almost two weeks. During this time, my teeth have already started to shift while waiting for retainers.

I was also told I would have a clinical review, but when I attended the appointment I was only scanned again and did not see a clinician.

As a result, after 2 months from the treatment my teeth have now returned to their initial position and I have still not received any response from the clinic.

In total for moderate package ended up 2.3k and have to pay £400 for retainers. Refinements cost £100 think pretty much everyone will have to get these. So it says less than a grand, you’ll end up paying about 3. I could not contact at all the phone doesn’t work and the email is really slow to reply. The set up isn’t professional I had my X-ray done in a box room and I had different dentists every time. Every app there was a different issue and they messed up the booking. I wanted refinements and bonding on my front teeth but by the end of my treatment I just left I didn’t want to deal with them anymore. I really wouldn’t say it’s worth it feels like you’ve gone in a back room of someone house not professional and too expensive. Also the consultations are about 5 minutes so each app I was driving over an hour to wait for 30-40 mins to be seen to go in for 5 minutes and leave. Everything is done on an app and automated there’s no care or personal feel I really wouldn’t recommend. If you want Invisalign specifically just go on their website it’s all through an app anyway you have to take all your progress pics yourself and tbh I don’t think anyone even looked at it
The WORST customer service once they’ve got you in

Everything was going well initially, but I ended up needing additional aligners because the comprehensive treatment wasn’t enough.

I was charged an extra £100 for this, even though I was told that refinements should be included in the comprehensive package.

I was first told the new aligners would arrive within 10 days. After chasing them multiple times by phone and email, I was then informed it would take 3–4 weeks. It’s now been 6 weeks, and I still haven’t received them.

I eventually got an email on a Tuesday saying the aligners had arrived at the clinic, but I could only collect them on Saturday or Sunday. I called and followed up twice to request an earlier collection, as I had already been waiting a long time, but received no response at all.

The offers may seem attractive, but the customer service is and the follow ups are very poor when you actually need support.

In 2018 I got three tattoos at the Hammersmith tattoo shop; made by Rob . Unfortunately, all of them healed with noticeable scarring and raised skin, especially in the areas with more ink (so in my case almost all of the tattoo). The texture becomes even more pronounced with heat or physical activity.

For comparison, I have other tattoos done by different artists on similar areas of my body that healed completely flat, so this does not seem to be a general skin issue.

I decided to write this review only now because I am currently considering laser removal and have had to look more closely at the condition of these tattoos and the scarring. I still have photos from the original sessions and the healing process, and the difference is quite clear.

While the designs of the tattoos themselves were fine (i drew the designs myself) the long-term result has been really disappointing due to the scarring and the raised skin.

I had a very disappointing and frustrating experience with Tax Resolute.

I signed a contract with Jesmin at a rate of £300 per hour after being introduced to her by my accountant. It was clearly agreed that my accountant would handle the accounting side, while Jesmin would liaise with HMRC.

However, after the contract was signed, she outsourced the work to someone else (Craig), who was charging her £200 per hour, while I was still billed £300 per hour. Throughout the case, Jesmin herself did not meaningfully contribute. I paid for her expertise, not for work to be passed on to someone else without transparency.

Because the contract was hourly-based, I believe the hours were significantly overstated. For example, even WhatsApp messages I sent that were never responded to were billed in 1-minute increments. This is completely unreasonable.

I requested a detailed timesheet in December 2024 and continued to chase it multiple times, but it was only provided in May 2025—by which point the total had already reached 95 hours. This made it impossible to properly monitor or challenge the billing as the work progressed.

I am disputing around 50 of those hours as they are clearly inflated and unsupported by evidence. In fact, they themselves admitted errors and removed 14 hours that they could not justify. Despite this, they continue to claim the remaining hours are substantiated, which I strongly disagree with. Even my accountant was shocked by the number of billable hours.

It appears that because Jesmin has already paid the outsourced worker, she is now attempting to pass those costs onto me without sufficient evidence. She has even tried to recover money from him, and when that failed, is now pursuing me instead.

To make matters worse, during the initial call before signing the contract, I was told the work would take approximately 50–60 hours. Yet the final bill nearly doubled that estimate at 95 hours.

Additionally, they have attempted to charge me for accounting work, which is completely unacceptable, as this was always meant to be handled by my accountant. This was clearly agreed in the initial meeting between myself, my accountant, Jesmin, and Craig.

My advice to others: NEVER agree to an hourly contract without strict oversight. If you do, insist on frequent and transparent timesheets throughout the engagement.

Overall, I feel misled, overcharged, and extremely dissatisfied with the service. Jesmin did not personally handle my case as expected, and the billing practices lack transparency and credibility.

**Your Best Car Successfully Sued**

In January 2022, myself and my wife agreed to purchase a Range Rover Sport from Your Best Car. Following the remote negotiations, I agreed to travel five and a half hours from our home in Chester to the Show yard in Cranbrook to collect the car and trade our 15 plate Range Rover in.

When I arrived, the salesman Jack, welcome me and we went to his office to de-register our number plate from our car and was helpful enough to give me access to his laptop to do so.

As all the documents were already completed by my wife before I arrived, I then went to check the car before I drove it home. When walking around I noticed that the tyre tread was low and it was clear that the tracking was out.

I explained to Jack that we would not accept the car in that condition and the tyre potentially ‘could’ be illegal. He refused to replace the tyre or credit me the equivalent value for a new one  and I explained that we were cancelling the deal. He said that our car was not in the condition that was described and would not oblige.

I requested our £500 deposit back and Jack very smuggly, insisted that we would not be getting it back as their ‘terms and conditions’ signed day my wife said that they would charge £495 to cancel the agreement and return the money to the finance company.

I returned home and confirmed with the finance company that there was not penalty to return the finance and emailed Your Best Car once again requesting the refund quoting ‘The Consumer Contracts (Information, cancelation and additional fees) Regulations 2013’ which states that the deposit must be returned otherwise we would move forward with a claim in the county courts.

We received a very bolshy response from Ashley from Your Best Car saying that they would not be returning the money and if we did pursued them to recover the money then they would counter clam for a further £495 plus compensation for their time to prepare the car.

We lodged our claim with the courts and sure enough Your Best Car issued their counter claim.

Following a few delays due to my wife's availability to attend a zoom hearing,  we attended a hearing on 10th July 2023, where we were successful in our claim and we were awarded our deposit back, plus the court and hearing fee.

The judge ruled that the clause in the Your Best Cars contract was unfair and unenforceable and made it very clear to the Managing Director Mr Woolger that it went against the Consumer Contract Regulations Act and threw out his pathetic (My view) counter claim.

It was unfortunate that we had to take Mr Woolger and Your Best Car to the small claims court to recover our rightful hard earned money, but delighted with the outcome.

We are concerned that there are no doubt other customers that have succumbed to this clause in the T’s & C’s and this is reason why we have decided to write this review. We have also contacted trading standards to inform them of the case and outcome.

I have no doubt that Your Best Car have had some very happy customers however Mr Woolger’s own LinkedIn profile states that his ‘goal is to build a reputable, recognised, modern brand within the motor industry centered on providing an 'outstanding customer experience, but from our particular experience, he has certainly failed to deliver this on occasion

We would encourage him and his team to remember his own business ethos in future disputed sales and will consider removing this clause from their contracts immediately so that no other customer is left out of pocket if they decide to cancel the agreement.

Attached is the picture of the tyre in question and the redacted documentation from the court proving our successful claim.

Please be very cautions when buying from this company and please check the T’s & C’s otherwise you may have to battle through the courts to get your money back!

Today my mother and I visited the Gymshark store in London to buy some new gym clothes. I’ve always been a fan of Gymshark, and my mother was excited to shop there for the first time as well. Unfortunately, the experience we had was extremely disappointing and honestly disheartening.

While we were browsing through the clothing and bags, one employee repeatedly kept telling us that the store was about to close. I completely understood and even responded politely that we were leaving. As I was making my way toward the exit from the first floor, I briefly stopped to look at a hoodie because I was considering coming back the next day to buy it. At that moment, the same employee came over again and said, “We’re literally closing.”

The way it was said felt very embarrassing and disrespectful, especially in front of my mother. We were not causing any trouble, and we were already heading out. Instead of feeling welcomed as customers, we felt rushed out of the store.

It’s unfortunate because I genuinely liked the brand, but after this experience, I no longer feel the same connection with Gymshark. A customer experience can make a huge difference, and sadly, this visit completely changed my perception of the brand.

Extremely POOR and unprofessional customer service!

The female staff member assigned to the fitting room demonstrated a consistently poor service attitude and a complete lack of understanding of the store’s inventory. When asked about the availability of a specific size, her repeated response was simply that the item was out of stock. I further asked whether the same item in a different color and size might be available for me to try on, yet she made no attempt to check the system or verify stock availability and immediately dismissed my request, stating that everything was already on the sales floor.
What made this situation even more unacceptable was that when I later went downstairs and checked the display racks myself, I clearly found two items in the exact size I needed. I then returned to the fitting room to question the same female staff member about why I had been told there was no stock when the items were visibly available. At this point, her attitude became even more unprofessional. Rather than acknowledging the mistake, she focused solely on defending herself, claiming that downstairs staff had told her there was no stock.
The male staff member standing beside her responded in the same dismissive and repetitive manner, insisting that “everything is on the racks,” which directly contradicted the earlier claim that there was no inventory. Their responses were poorly coordinated, illogical, and demonstrated a disturbing lack of accountability.
If your staff are unwilling or unable to assist customers with basic inventory checks, they should clearly state from the beginning that customers are expected to find sizes themselves on the sales floor. I would have had no issue with this approach if it had been communicated honestly. However, my dissatisfaction lies in the fact that the staff explicitly agreed to help look for the requested size but failed to execute this responsibility entirely.
Throughout this entire interaction, not a single apology was offered, nor was there any acknowledgment of inadequate job performance. The staff showed no awareness that their behavior was inappropriate. This refusal to accept responsibility, combined with a dismissive attitude toward customers, is both infuriating and unacceptable.
Furthermore, even after I pressed the service button in the fitting room, no staff member took appropriate action. Ultimately, I had to leave the fitting room area and seek help on my own before receiving any assistance.
I am deeply disappointed that a brand of your standing would tolerate such service standards. I left a negative Google review and was contacted by the clinic, who offered to see me again and try to resolve the issue. At that appointment, I also discussed improving my smile overall. I was offered veneers at what was described as a discounted price—£5,000 for eight teeth (including the tooth that was supposedly being corrected at no cost due to the gum issue).
I was told by Dr Bashar that they would need to trim the gum slightly and that the area above the implant would be replaced with a prosthetic piece designed to match the natural colour of my gums. At 25, I simply wanted the problem fixed and to feel confident in my smile.
Unfortunately, the result was not as promised. The prosthetic gum has never matched the colour of my natural gums. Now, four years later, I am once again experiencing issues. The gum around the area is receding and frequently inflamed, despite my best efforts to care for it.
I have since consulted another dentist, who advised that correcting this would require a gum graft—an expensive and lengthy procedure costing thousands.
While I am happy with my veneers and have had no issues with them, I can’t help but feel frustrated. As a now 30-year-old woman, I look back and feel I was a young and naive 18-year-old who trusted the process and ended up with a long-term issue that cannot be fully corrected without significant cost.

I contacted Burke Niazi Solicitors regarding a time-sensitive and urgent Court of Protection (COP) case. The initial contact was positive, they asked for a brief description of the issue and how we intended to finance the case. We explained the situation and confirmed we would require legal aid.

From that point on, the experience became extremely frustrating. All communication was handled via slow email, and phone calls were routinely ignored. As progress was not being made, we had to proactively organise a 14-day extension to the COP5 deadline ourselves because Anna was not moving things forward. This extension was approved by the opposing solicitor. Despite this additional time, we still ultimately missed the extended deadline because the solicitor took days to organise the legal aid documents. When we raised concerns about the approaching deadline, we were told that nothing could be done until legal aid was approved, leaving us with the choice to either wait or represent ourselves in court.

After missing the deadline, we were served documents for a court appearance later that month. At this stage, we were constantly chasing for updates from the solicitor, Anna, but received no responses to emails despite multiple follow-ups. Calling reception was equally unhelpful. On one occasion, after being put on hold, we were told they needed to check whether they were actually representing us and that they would get back to us. They never did, and this was already three weeks into communicating with Anna about the case via email. On other occasions, we were put on hold and told that we hadn’t been forgotten and that Anna was getting everything in order.

This went on for five weeks before we decided to seek representation elsewhere. We contacted Irwin Mitchell, and within just five days they had gathered all necessary details, arranged meetings, assigned solicitors and barristers, set court dates, prepared statements, collected documents, and submitted legal aid applications.

Then, out of nowhere, six weeks into the process and just one week before the court date, Anna emailed to say she was doing the finishing touches on the legal aid application. After all that time, they were still at step one. The handling of this case was completely unacceptable and disorganised. We informed them we no longer required their services.

We fully understand that firms can get busy. We contacted multiple firms before this, and some were upfront in letting us know they did not have the capacity to take on the case, which we appreciated. That happens. What was frustrating here is that this was not communicated to us. If they had been honest about their capacity from the start, we could have saved a significant amount of time and avoided a great deal of unnecessary stress.

I would highly recommend against using this firm if you require urgent Court of Protection assistance.

one_star_reviews.text: Horrible experience.

I have been a longstanding customer of Portman’s Pharmacy, dating back to when it was operated by the previous owners. During that time, the standard of service was consistently high—staff were attentive, personable, and demonstrated a genuine commitment to customer care. The pharmacy fostered a strong sense of community, with customers treated as individuals rather than transactions.

Since the change in management, however, there has been a noticeable and disappointing decline in service quality. Interactions have become impersonal, with a lack of courtesy and attentiveness that would reasonably be expected in a healthcare setting. The welcoming and patient-focused approach that once defined the pharmacy appears to have been lost.

Of particular concern is the apparent lack of regard for patient confidentiality in recent interactions. Pharmacies handle highly sensitive personal and medical information, and there is a clear professional and legal obligation to ensure that such information is treated with strict confidentiality. In the UK, this duty is governed by principles set out in the Data Protection Act 2018 and the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR), as well as professional standards enforced by the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC). Patients should be able to discuss their health and prescriptions in a manner that preserves their privacy and dignity. Any failure to maintain appropriate confidentiality standards represents a serious breach of trust and professional responsibility, which they are clearly failing to maintain.

As a provider of essential healthcare services, a pharmacy is expected to uphold high professional standards not only in the dispensing of medication but also in its duty of care toward patients. This includes treating customers with respect, ensuring clear and discreet communication, and maintaining a level of service consistent with regulatory expectations. Under UK consumer protection principles, including the Consumer Rights Act 2015, services should also be delivered with reasonable care and skill.

Regrettably, my recent experiences suggest that these standards are no longer being consistently met. This represents a significant departure from the level of service previously provided and undermines confidence in the pharmacy as a reliable healthcare provider.

In light of these concerns, I am unable to recommend this pharmacy in its current state and hope that appropriate steps will be taken to restore both the quality of service and the standards of confidentiality that patients are entitled to expect.

I am writing to formally raise a complaint regarding the conduct of the store manager, Joanna, at your Weekend Max Mara Marylebone High Street location.

I have been a loyal customer of your brand for several years, and until recently, my experiences have always been positive. However, I have now had multiple concerning interactions with Joanna that I feel must be addressed.

The first incident occurred following an in-store event, where I was assisted by a former employee, Sole, whose service was exceptional. During that visit, I purchased a crossbody bag. Upon returning home, I noticed that one of the screws on the bag was loose. When I returned to the store to request an exchange, Sole was not present, and I was instead assisted by Joanna.

Rather than offering a replacement or return, Joanna attempted to fix the issue herself using what appeared to be a kitchen knife. She insisted the bag was “repaired” and did not initially offer me the option of returning or exchanging it. When I raised a reasonable concern—that the screw might loosen again and the bag could be damaged or lost—her attitude changed noticeably. She appeared irritated, handled the situation abruptly, and instructed another employee to process a return in a dismissive manner before walking away.

Although I chose to overlook this incident at the time, a second experience on Saturday, 18 April 2026, was equally disappointing.

During this visit, I was assisted by Isabella, who was professional, attentive, and helpful throughout my shopping experience. However, while I was waiting for my items to be packaged at the checkout, Joanna intervened and began repeatedly checking the products multiple times. When I asked about this, Isabella explained that she had been instructed to do so, mentioning that there were ten items and that she needed to double-check them.

It was very clear that Isabella was under significant pressure. Her demeanor changed noticeably—she no longer appeared as confident and composed as she had been earlier while assisting me. Joanna’s tone of voice was also extremely loud and harsh, to the point that it felt more like shouting than speaking, and could easily be heard from outside the store. This created a very uncomfortable and tense atmosphere.

Additionally, I had left a pair of jeans for tailoring, as they were too long. Given that I had a very busy schedule the following week, I politely asked whether the item could be delivered to my home once the alterations were completed. Joanna’s response was a firm and immediate refusal. However, from Isabella’s reaction and expression, it seemed that such an option might have been possible. Due to the visible pressure placed on Isabella, I chose not to insist further, as I felt it might create additional difficulty for her.

As a customer, I found this overall behavior inappropriate and unprofessional. It not only negatively affected my experience, but also appeared to undermine and intimidate a staff member who had otherwise provided excellent service.

For your reference, I am an established and loyal client, and my purchase history—including my most recent transaction on 18 April 2026—can be verified in your system. You are also welcome to contact me directly using the details associated with my profile should you require any further information.

I believe that such conduct falls well below the standards expected from a managerial position, particularly within a brand that prides itself on customer care and professionalism.

I would appreciate it if you could investigate this matter and take appropriate steps to ensure a respectful and professional environment for both customers and staff.

I look forward to your response.

Kind regards,
Elena Patularu

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with VitalityHealth.

I requested authorisation for treatment for Thyroid Eye Disease in early February 2026. Despite having a Vitality GP referral and seeing their recommended ophthalmologist, they asked me to get my own NHS GP form, which I submitted three times, including specialist reports and GP forms. However, my claim remains pending for several weeks (12 weeks) with no clear decision, timeframe, or treatment pathway.

My condition was diagnosed as active, where early treatment is critical to prevent irreversible changes, including optic nerve compression and potential vision loss. Due to the delay and lack of authorisation, I was left with no option but to self-fund part of my treatment privately and continue care via the NHS.

In contrast, the care I received from Moorfields Eye Hospital (NHS) was prompt and excellent. I have since been referred to St Bartholomew’s Hospital (NHS) for radiotherapy as second-line treatment, again with minimal waiting time and an excellent clinical team.

Meanwhile, my private insurer has still not reached a decision, and the non-clinical customer service teams have been unable to coordinate effectively or involve an appropriate clinical review despite the urgency of the situation.

There appeared to be poor coordination between departments, repeated requests for information already provided, and a lack of clear accountability. Even after raising a formal complaint, responses have been slow and have not addressed the core issue of delayed clinical decision-making.

For a private health insurer, I expected a far more efficient and clinically responsive service—particularly for a time-sensitive condition.

I hope Vitality reviews its processes to ensure patients are not left without timely access to care.

Reply to Vitality Owner' response
Thank you for your response.
I have already contacted Vitality multiple times via phone, email and formal complaint channels over several weeks without resolution.
My concern has not been lack of contact, but the prolonged delay in authorisation and absence of a clear clinical decision or treatment pathway.
Given the nature of my condition and the urgency involved, I would expect this to be addressed through appropriate internal escalation rather than being redirected back to general customer service channels.
I would appreciate this being reviewed by the relevant clinical and authorisation teams, and for a clear written update to be provided to me as a priority.

Health insurance is supposed to give you peace of mind. Instead, this has been stressful, frustrating, and honestly feels like a complete let-down. I would urge anyone considering Vitality Healthcare to read the small print very carefully and think twice before assuming they will be there for you when you actually need to make a claim. For me, this has been a deeply disappointing experience.

I wasn’t demanding financial help, veterinary treatment, or for the charity to take them in - I was only asking for guidance on rehoming. The entire interaction felt dismissive, hostile and unnecessarily argumentative for absolutely no reason.

The most telling part of the call was that the woman’s attitude suddenly changed the moment I mentioned there were kittens involved as well. Only then did she appear remotely interested in listening. It left a very dishonest impression - as though the welfare of the mother cat alone was not worth basic courtesy or attention.

I ended the call feeling genuinely shocked at how disrespectful and unpleasant the interaction was. People contacting animal charities are often already stressed, worried, or trying to do the right thing in difficult circumstances. Basic patience, empathy and listening skills should be the bare minimum.

I sincerely hope calls are recorded for training and quality purposes, because the staff answering phones could benefit enormously from learning how to speak to people with a bit more professionalism and humanity.

If you're interested in the sixth form here please carefully consider your decision. I wouldn't want anyone to make the same mistakes we did with our son.
It markets itself as an inclusive music school and it really is. It bends over backwards to accommodate anyone with an issue of some sort. The problem is, if you don't have additional needs or you're not part of an underrepresented group, you're encouraged to let others have their own way. (It's unkind not to.)
But it's a miserable existence when you have no say in anything because a fellow 17 or 18-year old might cry if they can't choose the song you perform in your group, for example. I am not making that up - one student did cry because she was outvoted in her group and the tutor expected everyone else to cave in. It can be quite a manipulative environment in that sense, democracy doesn't really work. Everyone is entitled - but of course, someone has to bend.
If you're a boy, or a girl who doesn't have additional needs, it will be you and that pattern will be set.
My youngest child has SEND so I have no axe to grind on that front. Our approach has always been to work with the school to help him to do the work everyone else does and he's flying.
At the RS the preferred route seems to be exemptions. Some people miss certain lessons. They get given extensions constantly. They farm out the bits they can't do to others who can - great, they get the grade but what are they actually learning? The tutors know - one even made a joke about it in my son's class, asking 'are you actually going to do your own work today'?

Other students have already started to build music careers outside the RS are let off too. You have to perform on the other side of the world? That's okay, you go off when your coursework is due, don't worry. Then they wonder why nobody turns up during marked assessments.
If you just want to work hard and get on with things it's probably going to be tough for you here because your needs will most likely be low down in the pecking order. Rules don't seem to apply to everyone - but they probably will to you.
I have raised all this with the leadership and their response is that everyone has their own path to follow. It's what they tend to hide behind whenever you question them.
The great thing about it is they do give students a platform to perform and the time to work on their music skills. But they don't really show you how to do anything. You are just told what to do and you have to find a way through.
What my son has learned here is resilience, which is perhaps the greatest gift the RS could have given him. It is a tough old world out there - he's prepared for that now.

I rarely leave reviews, but I feel I have to share my experience so others know what to expect.
I recently entered into a car finance agreement with this dealership, and the entire process felt misleading from the start. The APR and terms were not clearly explained, and I later discovered commission details that were never properly disclosed. On top of that, the finance length was adjusted during the discussion in a way that made the monthly payments look more attractive, which I now believe was done to push the deal through.
Shortly after, I decided to withdraw from the agreement. I notified them clearly through email, WhatsApp, and phone calls. Despite this, the finance company has already raised a dispute with them to return the funds, which shows this situation is not straightforward.
What shocked me the most was the dealership’s behaviour after I cancelled:
I was told I would be charged a £499 “admin fee” just for withdrawing.
I received multiple calls from different staff, some saying the car would be delivered, others asking when I would pick it up — even after I clearly cancelled.
In one call, when I explained again that I had withdrawn, I was told about the £499 fee and the person hung up while laughing.
This level of unprofessionalism and pressure is completely unacceptable. Customers should be given clear, transparent information and treated with respect — not pushed into deals and then penalised for stepping back.
I strongly advise anyone considering buying from this dealership to:
Double-check every detail of the finance agreement
Ask directly about commission and total payable amount
Be very cautious if anything changes during the negotiation
I will be pursuing this further, as I do not believe these practices are fair or lawful.
Please be careful and make sure you fully understand what you are signing.
