We were referred to Elizavet by Snoots for x-rays for our dog. Our first impressions were very positive — the clinic was clean, the staff were friendly, and I initially felt comfortable leaving our little guy in their care.
However, the experience quickly became concerning. I dropped him off at 9:30am, but his x-rays were not done until 2:30pm, and I wasn’t able to collect him until 6pm. Nine hours in a crate for x-rays seems excessive, especially with no proactive updates from the clinic. I had to repeatedly call myself to find out what was happening.
When I arrived to collect him, the vet was informative and explained the x-rays thoroughly. Unfortunately, the rest of the experience was upsetting. When the nurse brought our dog out, he appeared extremely distressed and traumatised. When I expressed concern, it was dismissed as “just the effects of the anaesthesia,” despite him having undergone anaesthesia before without reacting this way.
I also asked whether he had been taken to the toilet during the nine hours he was there, and the nurse simply replied that she “wasn’t sure” because there was nothing in his crate. This response was alarming. Our dog smelled strongly of urine and his lead was wet with pee when he was returned to us.
What upset me most was the lack of empathy and care shown when these concerns were raised. After getting him out of the clinic he spent well over an hour crying, whimpering, and unable to settle, which made the whole experience incredibly stressful.
Overall, while the clinic made a good first impression, our experience left us very uncomfortable about the level of care our dog received. We would not recommend Elizavet to others and will not be returning.

I shall never use Voyage Prive again, and I suggest others AVOID it also. The booking process was very stressful as it took several days after payment for them to actually provide any confirmations or answer any of my questions. A scammer hacked into their database and contact me by Whatsapp asking for my card details to further confirm the holiday. Thankfully I didn't fall for it, but I don't think Voyage Prive's response to this hack/scammer was adequate. I got some kind of verbal apology on the phone but there was no goodwill gesture or anything else in recognition of the stress caused. And it gives the impression that their IT security can't be that strong/good, if they got hacked in the first place.

Their website mis-represented the location of the hotel, mis-advertised the availability of an eSIM, advertised the package booked as a 'private' tour but all excursions were in groups. The website looks shiny and professional, but behind the scenes it's clearly not as slick and the process caused me far more stress than if I'd just researched and booked everything directly and instantly myself. Voyage Prive comms channels don't work well, and I had long waits on the phone to try and resolve issues and get answers to key questions. Given the scammer hack on Whatsapp, I'd have expected something as simple as an an apology/goodwill gesture, but nothing. Absolute nightmare experience and a huge waste of money. Do not ever use Voyage Prive.

If I had any faith in this company then I'd try raising a complaint and requesting a partial refund due to the issues, but their Customer Service is so awful and stingy that I know they wouldn't engage with it or respond to a complaint.

We are absolutely disguted by their service and will be escalating this further.

Our cat Murphy became unwell on a Sunday evening. Due to his history of Hypokalemia, we wanted his potassium levels checked urgently to prevent him becoming seriously ill. We were told to arrive for 9:45pm (or earlier), so we arrived at 8:30pm.

Unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing from the start. The receptionist (Ruth, I believe) was abrupt and dismissive when we arrived, telling us she “didn’t have time” to check us in. After waiting 30 minutes, another staff member (Jodi) kindly triaged Murphy and placed him on oxygen as he was anxious and struggling to breathe.

We then waited around four hours with no updates, assuming tests were being carried out. Eventually, we were seen by the vet, who informed us no investigations had actually been done. Despite this, he immediately recommended overnight hospitalisation, oxygen, IV fluids, morphine and blood tests. When we asked whether blood tests could be done first before escalating treatment, we felt pressured into agreeing to the full hospitalisation package.

We were quoted approximately £950 for hospitalisation/testing and around £1500 total for treatment. Wanting to do what was best for Murphy, we reluctantly agreed despite having no insurance.

At 3am, the vet called to say Murphy’s potassium levels were fine but blood tests suggested a possible infection, so antibiotics would be given and oxygen removed. We were reassured he seemed brighter and improving.

However, the following morning communication became extremely confusing. We received conflicting information, including mention of a CT scan without explanation, and no one could clearly tell us why Murphy could not come home or what exactly was wrong with him. We practically begged to have him discharged so that we could take him to his usual vets but this ended up being a hassle/delay.

When Murphy was finally returned to us, he was lying in a carrier soaked with urine and faeces, despite notes showing this had happened hours earlier. More distressingly, he appeared significantly worse than when we brought him in and has continued to deteriorate since returning home.

The entire experience was traumatic. While some staff members were compassionate, the overall care felt disorganised, inconsistent and overwhelmed. We repeatedly received reassurance that Murphy was improving, so seeing his condition upon discharge was devastating.

We are left with several unanswered questions:

1. Why were we charged £1150 when we left without a diagnosis or treatment plan?
(Also the invoice appears to total to £933 so is there some sort of discrepancy here?)
2. Why was an infection suggested without certainty/conviction?
3. Why were bloods only taken ONCE despite Murphy’s history of rapidly changing potassium levels?
4. Why were multiple medications administered before a diagnosis was established?
5. Why were we not warned about the condition of his carrier so we could bring a clean one for transport home?

We visited on a beautiful evening, excited for a relaxing ride, but unfortunately left quite disappointed. The staff were friendly, helpful, and did their best throughout the trip. However, the condition of the canal was very poor, dirty, smelly, and filled with debris.

Our boat became entangled in garbage and other debris three separate times during the ride. The staff had to stop and clear it at the start, again during the 1-hour route, and once more during the 2-hour route. While they handled the situation professionally, the repeated stops significantly slowed the ride. For much of the trip, we were moving at less than half speed, making the experience far more tiring than enjoyable. We returned mid way and we didn't even have time to see the zoo area.

Before starting, we expressed concerns about the canal conditions and wanted to cancel, but were told that wasn't possible. We were also encouraged to take the 2-hour route and assured it would be worthwhile. Unfortunately, given the state of the canal, that was not our experience.

The staff deserve credit for their efforts, but the canal itself needs much better maintenance. I would not recommend the ride when the waterway is this dirty, as it significantly detracts from what should be a pleasant outing. This is not worth the money and time.

Only afterwards did someone finally call me saying that I “did not confirm” the appointment,  despite there being multiple messages from me confirming that I would attend.

No remorse, no sympathy for a client that has been with them for years despite the payments they kept taking after continuously vocalising that I was not satisfied with the progress.Horrible experience.

Don’t bother coming here, it’s based on greed.

I agreed on a total price of £1203.30 for my package, which included full body, face, and neck treatments. This price included a 60% promotion that was available at the time, as well as an additional 10% discount through a friend’s referral. The main reason I chose this clinic was because of this offer and the agreed price.

I only paid a £25  deposit at the beginning. Then I paid £306 for my first instalment and £345.67 for my second instalment. Based on this, the remaining balance should be around £539 . However, I was told that I still owe £1500 , and at one point they even mentioned a total of over £2000 . This makes no sense and is very concerning.

At first, they said there had been a misunderstanding and that one of their employees made a calculation mistake. I didn’t argue at the time. However, after a long time, I called again to confirm how much I had left to pay, as I believed I only had few more sessions remaining.

My package includes six sessions in total. So far, I have only had two sessions — full body twice and face & neck twice. Based on this, it is unclear how my remaining balance could suddenly increase to £1500 .

When I called, I was told that this is what shows in their system and that I would receive a response. However, they did not properly follow up and only asked me to communicate via email. I explained that I was worried and wanted clarification, as I started this package based on my budget. Being told I owe around £2000 or more  is extremely stressful and unacceptable.

During one of the calls, when I mentioned that I will leave a Google review, the representative laughed and hung up the phone. This behaviour was very unprofessional and disrespectful.

Overall, I am extremely disappointed with the customer service. The constant changes in pricing, lack of clear explanation, and dismissive attitude are unacceptable. This situation feels very misleading, and I would strongly advise others to be cautious before trusting this clinic.

I think this is potentially the worst restaurant I’ve ever been to. I’ve never written a bad review, I’ve always write good things but this is somewhere I MUST write something and hopefully the restaurant will choose to change.

We have had very good sashimi outside of London and so when we visited this place when we moved here, my husband and I were excited to try. When we got there, the service staff at the entrance was extremely inattentive and not helpful at all.

We explained we are here on a reservation under my husband name, she said ok and then she asked me if I’m allergic to anything. I said yes, and I responded to her about my allergies.
She said ok. She asked again what name did we reserve under, we replied again, she then once again asked me if I have allergies which… we were like what?

And I repeated myself again, then she asked again what’s the reservation name. At this point we were like what the hell is going on, but we decided to be nice because maybe English isn’t her first language. So we gave her the spelling of the name…. And then she asked me again if I have allergies…

Never mind right, so we went in and there are these fancy digital tables where you can view the menu and everything. She sat us down and asked if we wanted beer, we said yes and gave our beer order. She said okay, she will bring it over….. 20 mins later, nothing came… we asked for our beer, it was never registered… so we had to ask again.

The food options were extremely limited, I’ve never had sashimi option so little in my life but maybe this is just a London thing! So I was like ok… fine. I felt extremely cheated and also very very disappointed at the service.

I will not come back not only because of how shady the organisation is but also the menu and the horrible staff.

We had an extremely poor experience with this firm during our purchase of a property, and the whole process became far more stressful and draining than it should ever have been.

Our transaction went on for over 9 months and was plagued by repeated delays, contradictory communication, last-minute issues, and a real lack of proactive case management. It felt like we were constantly taking one step forward and two steps back.

Communication was a major issue throughout. We were often left feeling confused about what was actually happening, particularly around ongoing compliance checks. There was no clear or realistic timeframe given, and we were repeatedly asked for information we had already provided. The whole process felt unnecessarily complicated and overwhelming.

We also tried escalating our concerns, but it didn’t feel like management took meaningful action to resolve things or take control of the situation. This only added to our frustration and growing lack of confidence.

The individual handling our case is no longer with the firm, which added to the disruption and lack of continuity we experienced.

On top of everything, we incurred significant additional costs along the way, including compliance-related fees and insurance we were advised to put in place ready for completion — which ultimately didn’t go ahead. This added financial stress to an already difficult situation.

After months of uncertainty and stress, we made the difficult decision to move to another solicitor just to try and save the transaction. The new firm completed the purchase in just 5 weeks, which really highlights how poorly things had been handled previously.

This whole experience has been incredibly stressful, time-consuming, and emotionally draining. It has had a real impact on us over a long period of time.

We have now referred the matter to the Legal Ombudsman.

We would strongly advise others to avoid using this firm.

one_star_reviews.text:
Not impressed. I was enrolled with Embark through Barclays Wealth Management pension scheme and therefore anticipated a premium service.
Due to an unexpected change in my financial circumstances I needed to access my retirement funds at short notice.
Embark required a document of around 16-17 pages completing. A physical copy of the document then had to be posted to Embark. Embark then had a target of 11 working days to respond, which meant that each iteration required around 3 working weeks to complete at a time in my life where every day counted.
Once completed successfully I kept a copy of the successful documentation for future reference.
When I did require further funds I completed a new form based on the previous successful document only to find that the format of the document had changed with no notification to myself and I had to start again from scratch.
Barclays were willing to assist me in completing the forms successfully but for a fee of 1% of my total pension fund. Ultimately I was able to complete the form successfully at my first attempt after about an hour's work.
I ultimately transferred away from Embark to another company that only required an email from myself to make changes to my financial arrangements and typically implemented the changes successfully within a matter of days.
I understand that Embark have subsequently joined the 21st Century and will now accept the forms via email.
Their phone service was acceptable, providing me with updates as required when I rang them, rather than having to await the full 11 days plus postal time turnaround, hence the 1 star, as I would othewise have tried to give them zero stars.
They took a point in my life that was incredibly stressful and made it much worse, they seem to run the service to their own antiquated desires, rather than their clients requirements.
It is now mid May and have received my P60 for the previous financial year from the firm I swithched to, but am still awaiting my P60 for my previous year's pension from Embark.
